nodes.name: Speaker Building Energy
nodes.summary: Zoom push-in as speaker intensifies, mirroring the physical act of leaning forward when interest builds.

details.trigger: speech_energy_delta > +0.15 over 2s window (speaker getting more intense)
details.primary: zoom_push (slow push-in, 1.0x -> 1.1x over 3-4s) - camera 'leans in' as speaker builds
complements: music_energy should be rising or steady (not falling - energy mismatch)
caption style can shift to slightly larger/bolder if using kinetic captions
antiPatterns: Don't zoom if already zoomed past 1.2x (over-zoomed)
Don't zoom if time_since_last_zoom < 3s (too soon)
Don't add graphics during energy build - they interrupt momentum

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: zoom_push faster (2s), tighter target (1.15x)
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: skip zoom, let energy build speak for itself

details.why: Push-in narrows the viewer's world to the speaker. Mirrors the physical act of leaning forward when someone says something interesting. Blain Brown's motivated camera - motivation is 'this is becoming important.'
details.learningTarget: zoom speed and target scale per brand
details.detectionHint: compute rolling 2s derivative of speech_energy array. If > 0.15 for 1.5+ continuous seconds, trigger.

nodes.name: Speaker Energy Peak
nodes.summary: Quick zoom punch at peak speaker intensity to visually confirm the emotional climax the viewer anticipated.

details.trigger: speech_energy > (energy_baseline + 0.25) AND speech_energy_delta was positive, now flattening - speaker hit their highest intensity
details.primary: zoom_punch (quick snap to 1.2-1.3x over 0.3-0.5s)
complements: SFX subtle impact hit (low, felt not heard - -18dB or lower)
caption_emphasis on the current word (scale 130%, accent color)
antiPatterns: Don't zoom_punch if formality > 0.7 - feels aggressive. Use zoom_push instead
Don't zoom_punch more than zoom_budget allows
Don't pair with a transition - the punch IS the visual event, don't compete
Max 1 zoom_punch per 20 seconds

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: full zoom_punch (1.3x, 0.3s) + SFX + caption emphasis

details.why: The viewer's attention naturally peaks when the speaker's energy peaks. The zoom punch CONFIRMS the peak. Predictive processing: the viewer expected something big, the visual confirms it.
details.learningTarget: punch intensity (scale factor), whether SFX pairs well for this brand
details.detectionHint: find local maxima in speech_energy where value > energy_baseline + 0.25 AND preceding slope was positive.

nodes.name: Speaker Winding Down
nodes.summary: Gentle zoom pull-back and warm color shift as speaker energy softens, allowing the viewer's body to release tension.

details.trigger: speech_energy_delta < -0.2 over 2s AND speaking_rate dropping > 15% - speaker is getting quieter and slower (reflective, concluding)
details.primary: zoom_pull_back (gentle return toward 1.0x, or slight pull to 0.95x over 3-5s)
complements: color_warm_shift (+100-200K, subtle - warmth = comfort as energy settles)
if zoomed in, this is the natural moment to return to neutral framing
antiPatterns: Don't add graphics - this is a breathing moment
Don't add SFX - silence or ambient only
Don't cut away during wind-down - let the moment complete

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: hold on speaker's face (this wind-down IS the emotional climax - vulnerability)
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: minimal response, just ensure no competing visual elements

details.why: Pearlman's exhale. The viewer's body releases tension as the speaker softens. Adding visual stimulation fights the natural rhythm.
details.learningTarget: whether warm shift is appropriate for this brand's aesthetic
details.detectionHint: speech_energy_delta < -0.2 sustained 1.5s+ AND speaking_rate < baseline * 0.85

nodes.name: Speaker Emphasis Word
nodes.summary: Visual caption emphasis on speaker-stressed words to confirm auditory emphasis through dual-coding.

details.trigger: emphasis_word = true (volume spike > 1.5x local avg + duration > 110%)
details.primary: caption_emphasis (scale word 120-140%, accent color, optional pop animation)
complements: zoom_drift (very subtle 1.0x -> 1.05x aligned to the word)
antiPatterns: Don't emphasize more than 1 word per 8-10 seconds (emphasis fatigue)
Don't emphasize filler words even if volume spikes on them
Don't pair emphasis with stat_graphic on the same word - visual competition

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: pop animation + scale 140% + accent color + subtle zoom
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: accent color only, no scale change

details.why: The speaker stressed this word for a reason. Visual emphasis confirms what the ear heard. Dual-coding: auditory emphasis + visual emphasis = stronger memory encoding.
details.learningTarget: emphasis frequency (how many per minute feels right), animation style
details.detectionHint: word-level amplitude analysis. Flag words where amplitude > 1.5 * rolling_avg(surrounding 5 words) AND duration_ms > 1.1 * avg_word_duration.

nodes.name: Speaker Rhetorical Pause
nodes.summary: Protect deliberate mid-thought silence by holding the shot and doing nothing, letting the pause serve as emphasis.

details.trigger: speech_energy was > 0.5 AND silence_duration > 500ms AND next sentence continues same topic (not topic_boundary) - speaker paused deliberately mid-thought for emphasis
details.primary: hold (do nothing - the pause IS the technique)
complements: caption: show '...' or hold last word visible
very subtle ambient sound swell (room tone +2dB for 1s)
antiPatterns: NEVER remove this silence - it's intentional
Don't add SFX, graphics, or any visual element
Don't cut during the pause

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: extended hold, let pause run its full natural duration
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: trim to 800ms (keep the beat but don't drag)

details.why: Strategic silence after a strong statement lets the idea land. The viewer's brain uses the pause to process.
details.learningTarget: max pause duration per context
details.detectionHint: silence_duration > 500ms AND speech_energy[-1] > 0.5 AND NOT topic_boundary_next AND NOT filler_before_silence

nodes.name: Speaker Speeding Up
nodes.summary: Increase edit density to match accelerating speaker pace, entraining the visual rhythm to the vocal rhythm.

details.trigger: speaking_rate_wpm > baseline * 1.2 sustained for 5+ seconds
details.primary: increase_edit_density (shorten shot holds by 20%, allow faster cuts)
complements: if listing items: consider quick graphic per item
caption speed should match - faster reveal
antiPatterns: Don't increase density if visual_complexity is already high - cognitive overload
Don't fight the speaker's rhythm with slow, held shots

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: match speaker's pace fully, dense edits, jump cuts OK

details.why: The viewer's internal rhythm entrains to the speaker's rhythm. When the speaker accelerates, the visual should follow.
details.learningTarget: how aggressively to match speaker pace per brand
details.detectionHint: rolling 10s average of speaking_rate_wpm > baseline * 1.2 -> reduce active pacing_tolerance.

nodes.name: Speaker Slowing For Gravity
nodes.summary: Hold the shot longer with imperceptible push-in when speaker deliberately slows with sustained energy, signaling deep importance.

details.trigger: speaking_rate < baseline * 0.75 AND pitch_contour = falling AND speech_energy stable or rising - slowing down but NOT losing energy - deliberate, grave, important
details.primary: hold_shot_longer (extend by pacing_tolerance * 0.5)
complements: zoom_push (very slow, 1.0x -> 1.08x over 5-6s - almost imperceptible)
music: should be at lowest energy or ducked further
antiPatterns: Don't cut during this - the speaker chose this pace intentionally
Don't add graphics (compete with the gravity)
Distinguish from 'speaker losing train of thought' - key: energy stays stable or rises

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: full hold, imperceptible push, this IS the climax

details.why: When someone slows down and gets quieter but MORE intense, they're saying something that matters deeply. Tarkovsky's time-pressure.
details.learningTarget: how far past pacing_tolerance to hold
details.detectionHint: speaking_rate < baseline * 0.75 AND speech_energy >= energy_baseline AND pitch_contour = falling.

nodes.name: Filler Removal
nodes.summary: Remove detected speech fillers in Mode 2 footage with zoom masking for jump cuts and audio crossfades.

details.trigger: filler_detected = true in Mode 2 raw footage
details.primary: silence_removal (cut the filler, close the gap)
complements: if removing creates a jump cut: add subtle zoom change (+/-5% scale) to mask
if removing creates audio pop: 50ms crossfade at splice
antiPatterns: Don't remove fillers if formality < 0.3 (casual content where fillers feel natural)
Don't remove so aggressively that speech sounds robotic

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - quality operation, not creative
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - quality operation, not creative
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - quality operation, not creative

details.why: Fillers reduce perceived speaker competence (Brennan & Williams 1995). In professional content, they signal unpreparedness.
details.learningTarget: aggressiveness per brand
details.detectionHint: already exists in raw-footage-processor.ts.

nodes.name: Emotional Shift Detected
nodes.summary: Bridge emotional valence transitions with color, music, and pacing adjustments to prevent cognitive dissonance at mood shifts.

details.trigger: emotional_valence changes (positive -> negative or vice versa) over 3-5s window
details.primary: transition_bridge (don't hard-cut across an emotional shift)
complements: color_shift (warm->cool if positive->negative, +/-100-150K)
music_crossfade (fade toward matching mood)
pacing adjustment (negative = slightly slower, positive = slightly faster)
antiPatterns: Don't use jarring transitions (zoom punch, flash) at emotional boundaries
Don't let music contradict new valence for more than 3 seconds

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: full bridge treatment (color + music + pacing all adjust)

details.why: Emotional shifts are the most memorable moments. Mismatched editing during a shift creates cognitive dissonance.
details.learningTarget: bridge duration and intensity
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] for accurate voice-level detection. Track emotional_valence over rolling 5s window.

nodes.name: Quantitative Claim
nodes.summary: Display stat graphic for assertive numeric claims using dual-coding for 2x retention, sourcing text only from transcript.

details.trigger: entity_number = true AND claim_strength = assertive or factual
details.primary: stat_graphic - display EXACT number from transcript (never AI-generated), format cleaned ('three hundred percent' -> '300%'), style matches formality level, position: lower third or center never overlapping caption zone, duration: 2-4s (enter 0.3s after number is spoken, hold, exit)
complements: zoom_push (slow, adds visual weight)
caption_emphasis (accent color on number word)
subtle SFX on graphic entrance (not on every number)
antiPatterns: NEVER hallucinate graphic text - source ONLY from transcript or brief
Don't for trivial numbers ('my 2 cats' doesn't need a graphic)
Don't if claim_strength = hedged (see hedged_statement_restraint)
Don't if active_overlays_count >= 2
Don't within 3s of another graphic

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: animated counter + zoom + SFX + caption emphasis
weightResponse.medium: 0.6-0.8: standard stat graphic + zoom_push; 0.4-0.6: standard stat graphic, no complements
weightResponse.low: 0.2-0.4: caption_emphasis only, no separate graphic; 0.2-: skip visual treatment

details.why: Dual-coding theory (Paivio 1971) - visual + auditory encoding of same data -> 2x retention.
details.learningTarget: graphic style, size, animation type, SFX inclusion per brand
details.detectionHint: NER detects numeric entity -> check claim_strength -> check moment_weight -> select tier -> compute position -> schedule entry.

nodes.name: Hedged Statement Restraint
nodes.summary: Block stat graphics for uncertain numeric claims to prevent editorial dishonesty through visual amplification of hedged statements.

details.trigger: claim_strength = hedged AND entity_number = true - uncertain about a number: 'maybe around 200' or 'could be up to 50%'
details.primary: NO stat_graphic (visual amplification of hedged claim feels dishonest)
complements: caption only - standard treatment, no emphasis
antiPatterns: NEVER show stat graphic for hedged claim

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - integrity constraint

details.why: If speaker says 'might be around 300%' and video shows big animated '300%', the content is MORE certain than the speaker intended. Editorial dishonesty.
details.learningTarget: N/A - hard rule
details.detectionHint: claim_strength = 'hedged' is a BLOCKING condition on quantitative_claim. If hedged, skip entirely.

nodes.name: Name Or Brand Mentioned
nodes.summary: Show lower third on first mention of a person, company, or product name for visual reinforcement of auditory information.

details.trigger: entity_name = true (person, company, product name in transcript)
details.primary: lower_third (name, title/role if available from brief) - first mention only, enter: 0.5s after spoken, duration: 3-5s, exit: fade
antiPatterns: Don't repeat for same name within 60 seconds
Don't show if name is the speaker themselves
Text from transcript or brief only
Don't show during montage_mode

weightResponse.high: 0.7+: animated lower_third (brand styled)

details.why: Names mentioned once in speech are easily missed. Visual reinforcement ensures the viewer catches the reference.
details.learningTarget: which name types warrant lower thirds per brand
details.detectionHint: NER -> filter PERSON/ORG/PRODUCT -> check first mention -> schedule at word timestamp + 500ms.

nodes.name: Call To Action
nodes.summary: Full CTA treatment in final 20% of video with zoom, graphic, and music resolution to maximize conversion at peak viewer commitment.

details.trigger: entity_CTA = true AND position_in_video > 0.7
details.primary: zoom_in (slow push, 1.0x -> 1.15x, 3-4s)
complements: lower_third_CTA (CTA text from brief: URL, 'Subscribe', etc.)
music: resolving (final chord, sustained note)
antiPatterns: Don't add distracting SFX
Don't add busy graphics
Don't zoom if already at 1.2x+
Don't place CTA in unsafe zone (bottom 20%)

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: zoom + CTA graphic + music resolution + subtle chime SFX

details.why: CTA in final quarter correlates with higher conversion (Wistia: 16% avg CTA conversion rate). Zoom creates intimate direct address. Music resolution primes action.
details.learningTarget: CTA style, zoom intensity, hard vs soft CTA per brand
details.detectionHint: imperative verb in final 25% of transcript -> check entity_CTA -> if position > 0.7, trigger.

nodes.name: Call To Action Early
nodes.summary: Minimal emphasis for CTAs in the first 70% of video to avoid premature 'sold to' feeling before value delivery.

details.trigger: entity_CTA = true AND position_in_video < 0.7
details.primary: caption_emphasis (accent color + slight scale on CTA phrase)
complements: subtle zoom_drift (1.0x -> 1.05x)
antiPatterns: Don't use full CTA treatment mid-content (feels premature/pushy)
Don't show CTA lower_third (save for end)

weightResponse.high: 0.7+: caption emphasis + subtle zoom

details.why: Early CTAs perform worse. Over-emphasis makes viewer feel 'sold to' before receiving value.
details.learningTarget: whether brand uses mid-content CTAs deliberately
details.detectionHint: same detection, fires when position < 0.7. Lower priority.

nodes.name: Rhetorical Question Beat
nodes.summary: Brief visual pause after rhetorical questions exploiting the Zeigarnik Effect to create cognitive tension that drives retention.

details.trigger: rhetorical_question = true
details.primary: beat_pause (0.3-0.8s visual 'moment' - hold, let question land)
complements: zoom_push (subtle, 1.0x -> 1.05x during question)
hold question text in captions 0.5s longer than speech duration
antiPatterns: Don't answer the question visually before the speaker does
Don't cut during or immediately after
Don't add graphics during the question

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: extended pause (0.8s) + zoom + caption hold

details.why: Zeigarnik Effect - unresolved questions create cognitive tension that drives retention.
details.learningTarget: pause duration
details.detectionHint: sentence ends with '?' + next sentence > 300ms later + speech_energy not falling.

nodes.name: Topic Shift
nodes.summary: Visual reset at topic boundaries with zoom return and optional chapter treatment, mirroring the brain's cognitive reset at goal-shifts.

details.trigger: topic_boundary = true AND silence_duration > 400ms
details.primary: visual_reset - zoom_reset to 1.0x if currently zoomed (1-2s ease), consider new shot/angle if available (Mode 2 multi-camera), subtle transition beat (0.2-0.3s)
complements: align with music section boundary if nearby
ambient crossfade
MAJOR shift (cosine delta > 0.5): chapter-style treatment (brief fade or title card)
antiPatterns: Don't dip-to-black for minor shifts (too heavy)
Don't add graphics at exact boundary (let new topic establish first)
Don't hold zoom from previous topic into new one

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: full reset + chapter treatment if large delta

details.why: Event segmentation theory (Zacks) - brain expects perceptual reset at goal-shift boundaries. The zoom reset mirrors the cognitive reset.
details.learningTarget: chapter threshold - how large a shift warrants chapter treatment
details.detectionHint: embedding cosine similarity < 0.7 between consecutive sentences + silence > 400ms.

nodes.name: Strong Claim Emphasis
nodes.summary: Subtle zoom push and caption emphasis for assertive non-numeric claims, with optional quote card for standout assertions.

details.trigger: claim_strength = assertive AND speech_energy > energy_baseline AND NOT entity_number
details.primary: zoom_push (slow, 1.0x -> 1.1x, 2-3s)
complements: caption_emphasis (key phrase in bold or accent color)
if quote-worthy: quote_card with cleaned assertion text from transcript
antiPatterns: Don't zoom_punch on claims (too aggressive - feels propagandistic)
Max 2-3 quote_cards per video
Text must be cleaned from transcript, never AI-editorialized

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: zoom + quote card + caption emphasis

details.why: Subtle emphasis confirms importance without overselling. Zoom_push (conviction) vs zoom_punch (forcing) - push feels like agreement, punch feels like propaganda.
details.learningTarget: quote_card frequency and style per brand
details.detectionHint: claim_strength = 'assertive' -> NOT entity_number -> check moment_weight -> apply.

nodes.name: High Motion Fast Pacing
nodes.summary: Shorten shot holds for high-motion non-speech footage since motion provides enough stimulation for faster processing.

details.trigger: motion_intensity > 0.7 sustained 2+ seconds AND speech_energy < 0.3 - lots of visual action, no speech (B-roll, action footage)
details.primary: shorten_shot_hold (reduce pacing_tolerance by 30-40%)
complements: hard cuts preferred (motion provides continuity across cuts)
beat-sync cuts if music present
antiPatterns: Don't hold high-motion footage for long durations (repetitive after 3-4s)
Don't dissolve between high-motion shots (chaotic blend)
Don't add text overlays on high-motion footage (unreadable)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: very fast cuts (1-2s), metric montage if music available

details.why: High motion provides enough stimulation that viewers process shots faster. Fast cuts FEEL right because each cut provides new information.
details.learningTarget: optimal shot duration for high-motion per brand
details.detectionHint: rolling 2s average of motion_intensity > 0.7 AND speech_energy < 0.3 -> reduce active pacing_tolerance.

nodes.name: Low Motion Visual Interest
nodes.summary: Apply imperceptible zoom drift on static talking-head shots to prevent visual habituation without creating false excitement.

details.trigger: motion_intensity < 0.2 AND time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance * 0.7 AND speech_energy > 0.3 - static shot with active speech, approaching hold limit (talking head)
details.primary: zoom_drift (very subtle, 1.0x -> 1.05x or back, 5-8s)
complements: caption animation provides secondary visual movement
antiPatterns: Don't zoom_punch to create false excitement
Don't add unmotivated transitions
Don't fight the content's natural energy

weightResponse.high: Not strongly weight-dependent - maintenance technique

details.why: The eye needs motion to maintain engagement. Even 2-3% zoom over 8s prevents visual habituation. The viewer doesn't notice - they just don't get bored.
details.learningTarget: zoom drift speed and amount
details.detectionHint: motion_intensity < 0.2 AND time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance * 0.7 -> apply subtle drift.

nodes.name: Cut On Action
nodes.summary: Hard cut at the peak of visible motion making the edit invisible because the brain tracks trajectory through the splice.

details.trigger: motion_intensity peaks (local max > 0.6) AND action boundary detected
details.primary: hard_cut at peak of action (+/- 2 frames of motion peak)
complements: continuous ambient across the cut
antiPatterns: Don't cut BEFORE peak (premature)
Don't cut > 5 frames AFTER peak (late)
Don't use transition effects - hard cut preserves momentum

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - mechanical technique

details.why: Murch: 'cut on movement.' When the eye tracks motion, a cut during motion is invisible - the brain is tracking trajectory and doesn't notice the frame change.
details.learningTarget: N/A - physics-based
details.detectionHint: find local maxima in motion_intensity > 0.6 -> score by proximity to speech boundaries. [PHASE_2] V-JEPA provides action segmentation.

nodes.name: Shot Scale Monotony Break
nodes.summary: Vary shot scale after 3 consecutive identical scales to provide the eye with new spatial information and prevent visual monotone.

details.trigger: shot_scale same for 3+ consecutive shots
details.primary: vary_shot_scale on next cut (at least 1 step different)
complements: wider shot: slightly longer hold. Tighter shot: slightly shorter hold
antiPatterns: Don't jump > 2 steps (ECU to WS is jarring unless motivated)
Don't alternate robotically (MCU-WS-MCU-WS feels like seesaw)
Only apply when system controls shot selection (Mode 1 storyboard or Mode 2 multi-camera)

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - rhythm/variety constraint

details.why: Three identical shot scales create visual monotone. Varying scale gives the eye new spatial information.
details.learningTarget: variation amount per brand - some want consistent, some want dynamic
details.detectionHint: track shot_scale per segment -> if last 3 identical -> flag for next.

nodes.name: Color Temperature Continuity
nodes.summary: Block dissolves between shots with >1000K color temperature difference to prevent ugly mid-frame blends from simultaneous contrast.

details.trigger: color_temperature delta > 1000K between consecutive shots at cut point
details.primary: if hard_cut planned: acceptable (cut separates color worlds). if dissolve planned: BLOCK dissolve, use opaque transition (hard cut, dip-to-black, or wipe)
antiPatterns: NEVER dissolve between > 1000K delta - mid-frames create ugly blend

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - quality constraint

details.why: Albers' simultaneous contrast. In dissolve, viewer sees BOTH color worlds. If clashing, blend is muddy.
details.learningTarget: N/A - perception constraint
details.detectionHint: avg color_temp of last 10 frames of clip A vs first 10 of clip B -> if delta > 1000K AND dissolve -> switch transition.

nodes.name: AI Artifact Prevention
nodes.summary: Preventively cut AI-generated footage before temporal degradation becomes visible, finding best cut points before artifact onset.

details.trigger: ai_artifact_risk > 0.5 AND time_since_last_cut > 2.5s
details.primary: cut_early (cut 0.5-1s BEFORE artifact becomes visible) - find best cut point: speech boundary > motion peak > beat > arbitrary
complements: flash or whip-pan can mask boundary if hard cut would be jarring
speed_ramp: if no good cut point, brief 1.3-1.5x for 0.5s to compress degrading zone
antiPatterns: NEVER hold AI footage past 5s without narrative_pressure > 0.8
NEVER slow-mo AI footage - amplifies artifacts
Preventive, not reactive

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: tolerate up to 4s if narratively critical

details.why: AI models maintain quality for 3-4s, then degrade. Cutting before degradation = preventive quality control.
details.learningTarget: per-model artifact onset timing
details.detectionHint: frame-to-frame diff + face landmark stability -> if trending up past threshold AND time > 2.5s -> find nearest cut point.

nodes.name: Face Emotion Music Alignment
nodes.summary: Flag mood mismatches between visible face emotion and music mood for review, without auto-correcting potentially intentional contrast.

details.trigger: face_emotion strong (not neutral) AND music mood contradicts
details.primary: flag_mood_mismatch (don't auto-correct - flag for review)
complements: if AI-selected music: suggest mood shift
if user-selected: flag but don't change
antiPatterns: Don't auto-swap music - mismatch sometimes intentional (ironic, comedic)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: stronger flag

details.why: Cross-modal binding - conflicting face/music signals create confusion.
details.learningTarget: whether brand uses intentional contrast
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] requires face_emotion. Until then, low-confidence flag only.

nodes.name: Screen Direction Continuity
nodes.summary: Flag 180-degree rule violations when screen direction flips between consecutive shots without motivated camera movement.

details.trigger: screen_direction flips between consecutive shots without motivated camera movement
details.primary: flag_continuity_break - Mode 1: adjust prompt for incoming shot. Mode 2: prefer alternative take with correct direction, or add buffer shot
antiPatterns: Don't ignore in dialogue/interview (viewer loses spatial orientation)
Don't over-enforce in montage/fast-cut (spatial continuity less important)

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - continuity constraint

details.why: 180-degree rule. Screen direction consistency maintains the viewer's mental spatial map.
details.learningTarget: N/A - perceptual constraint
details.detectionHint: [NEEDS_CODE] face orientation + optical flow -> compare across cuts -> flag if flipped.

nodes.name: Cut On Downbeat
nodes.summary: Align cuts to musical downbeats exploiting neural entrainment, with humanization skips after 4 consecutive beat-locked cuts.

details.trigger: music_beat = downbeat AND time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance * 0.6
details.primary: align_cut_to_beat (snap to nearest downbeat, +/- 3 frames)
complements: if speech active: speech boundary takes priority over beat
antiPatterns: Don't beat-lock every cut
After 4+ consecutive beat-aligned cuts: skip next alignment (humanize)
Speech boundaries ALWAYS override beats

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: tight beat lock (+/- 1 frame)

details.why: Neural entrainment (Large & Palmer 2002) - cuts on beats feel 'right.' But perfect sync too long sounds robotic.
details.learningTarget: beat-lock precision and skip frequency per brand
details.detectionHint: from beat_positions, find nearest downbeat to each cut point -> snap if within threshold AND consecutive_beat_cuts < 4.

nodes.name: Music Section Transition
nodes.summary: Align the most significant visual transition to music section changes, adjusting edit density to track musical architecture.

details.trigger: music_section changes (verse -> chorus, build -> drop, etc.)
details.primary: align_visual_transition (most significant visual change should coincide with music section change) - slide nearby scene transitions to align within +/-0.5s
complements: verse -> chorus: increase edit density, more zoom, more graphics
chorus -> verse: decrease density, pull back, fewer overlays
build -> drop: zoom_punch or flash at exact drop frame + impact SFX
any -> outro: begin visual resolution, pull-back, remove overlays
antiPatterns: Don't fight the music structure
Don't maintain same density across section change
Don't gentle dissolve at a hard drop (energy mismatch)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: dramatic section alignment

details.why: Music has architecture. Viewer EXPECTS visual energy to track musical energy.
details.learningTarget: how dramatic the visual response should be per section change
details.detectionHint: from music_section transitions -> find nearest visual change -> slide timing within +/-0.5s. Drops: align within +/-2 frames.

nodes.name: Music Drop Impact
nodes.summary: Frame-accurate zoom punch or flash at music drops using synchresis to make the viewer physically feel the beat.

details.trigger: music_section = 'drop' AND previous section was 'build' or 'breakdown'
details.primary: zoom_punch (1.2-1.3x, 0.2-0.3s - frame-accurate to first beat of drop) OR flash_transition (2-4 frame white flash leading into drop)
complements: SFX impact hit (low-frequency boom)
montage_mode kicks into highest density if active
antiPatterns: 3+ frames off timing = impact feels disconnected
Don't use both zoom_punch AND flash - pick one
Max 2-3 drops per video get this treatment

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: zoom punch + SFX + flash

details.why: Synchresis: visual impact + audio impact at same frame = viewer FEELS the drop physically.
details.learningTarget: zoom_punch vs flash preference, SFX inclusion
details.detectionHint: music_section == 'drop' AND previous was 'build'/'breakdown' -> align to first beat +/- 2 frames.

nodes.name: Music Energy Tracking
nodes.summary: Adjust edit density proportionally to music energy changes, shortening holds when energy rises and lengthening when it falls.

details.trigger: music_energy delta > 0.2 over 4s window
details.primary: adjust edit_density proportionally - rising: shorten holds. falling: lengthen holds
complements: rising: increase zoom/SFX/graphic likelihood
falling: decrease overlays, simplify, wider shots
antiPatterns: Speech pacing takes priority if speech present
Only respond to significant sustained changes (> 0.2 delta over 4s)

weightResponse.high: music_primary = true: music energy fully drives pacing
weightResponse.medium: music_primary = false: 30% weight to speech signals
weightResponse.low: music_primary = false: 30% weight to speech signals

details.why: Music and visual pacing should move together. Rising music with static visuals = unfulfilled tension.
details.learningTarget: loose vs tight coupling per brand
details.detectionHint: rolling 4s music_energy average -> compare to previous 4s -> if delta > 0.2, adjust pacing.

nodes.name: Ambient Continuity At Cuts
nodes.summary: Ensure ambient crossfade at every cut to prevent true silence which the brain interprets as 'the audio broke.'

details.trigger: every hard cut or transition
details.primary: ambient_crossfade (0.1-0.3s overlap)
complements: scene_type change (indoor->outdoor): longer crossfade (0.3-0.5s) or designed transition sound
same scene_type: short crossfade (0.1-0.2s)
antiPatterns: NEVER true silence at a cut - technical error
Don't let ambient level pump at cuts
Exception: narrative_pressure > 0.6 -> ambient can be very low but must exist (-40dB minimum)

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - technical quality

details.why: Chion: true silence doesn't exist in nature. The brain interprets it as 'the audio broke.'
details.learningTarget: N/A - hard quality requirement
details.detectionHint: at every cut -> verify ambient level >= -45dB in both clips -> if not, insert crossfade or room tone.

nodes.name: Audio Ducking Under Speech
nodes.summary: Deterministic music ducking during speech to prevent frequency masking in the 200Hz-4kHz overlap range.

details.trigger: speech_energy > 0.2 AND music_energy > 0.3
details.primary: duck_music [DETERMINISTIC] - Duck amount: -6 to -12 dB. Attack: 200-400ms. Release: 400-800ms. Look-ahead: 100-200ms. Under speech: -18 to -24 dB. Solo: -12 to -6 dB.
antiPatterns: Don't duck so aggressively music disappears
Don't duck with < 100ms attack (audible pump)
Don't leave music unducked during speech

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - always applied

details.why: Frequency masking - speech and music overlap 200Hz-4kHz. Both at similar levels = neither heard clearly.
details.learningTarget: duck amount and timing per brand
details.detectionHint: already exists in ducking pipeline. Verify parameters match specs.

nodes.name: Hook Zone Treatment
nodes.summary: Ensure strong visual opening in first 5% of video since 20-30% of viewers leave within 5 seconds.

details.trigger: position_in_video < 0.05
details.primary: ensure_strong_opening - first frame must be visually compelling (not black, not blank), first 2 seconds: visual motion, a face, or intriguing composition, speech should start within 1-2 seconds
antiPatterns: NEVER start with logo/intro > 2 seconds
NEVER start with 'Hey guys, welcome to...'
Don't start with least interesting part and build up
Don't fade-from-black > 0.5s

weightResponse.high: Opening is ALWAYS high weight (0.8+) regardless of moment_weight_map - survival zone
weightResponse.medium: Opening is ALWAYS high weight (0.8+) regardless of moment_weight_map - survival zone
weightResponse.low: Opening is ALWAYS high weight (0.8+) regardless of moment_weight_map - survival zone

details.detectionHint: position < 0.05 -> verify first frame not black -> verify hook within 2s -> verify no long bumper.

nodes.name: Closing Zone Treatment
nodes.summary: Visual resolution in final 15% with slowing pace, neutral framing return, and end card preparation for psychological closure.

details.trigger: position_in_video > 0.85
details.primary: visual_resolution - pacing slows slightly, pull-back to neutral framing if zoomed, prepare for end card
complements: music entering outro. If not, begin fade
remove non-essential overlays
if loop_structure = true: last frame connects to first frame
antiPatterns: Don't maintain peak energy into last 5%
Don't introduce new visual elements in closing
Don't end abruptly without resolution

weightResponse.medium: Closing zone follows its own rhythm - weight modulates CTA intensity
weightResponse.low: Closing zone follows its own rhythm - weight modulates CTA intensity

details.learningTarget: closing pace, end card style per brand
details.detectionHint: position > 0.85 -> begin resolution -> schedule end card at -3 to -5s from end.

nodes.name: Pacing Tolerance Exceeded
nodes.summary: Find optimal cut point when shot hold exceeds pacing tolerance without narrative pressure, prioritizing speech boundaries.

details.trigger: time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance AND narrative_pressure < 0.5
details.primary: find_cut_point (priority: speech clause boundary > motion peak > beat > arbitrary)
complements: reset zoom at the cut
if topic_boundary nearby (within 2s): extend hold to reach it (cleaner cut)
antiPatterns: NEVER cut mid-word
NEVER cut mid-action (unless cut-on-action)
Don't metronomic cut - natural variation essential
If narrative_pressure > 0.5: IGNORE this mapping - hold is intentional

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - pacing_tolerance already modulated by genre_parameters
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - pacing_tolerance already modulated by genre_parameters
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - pacing_tolerance already modulated by genre_parameters

details.detectionHint: time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance -> check narrative_pressure -> if < 0.5, scan forward for best cut.

nodes.name: Edit Density Correction
nodes.summary: Adjust upcoming pacing when cumulative edit density diverges >25% from target to maintain viewer-entrained edit rhythm.

details.trigger: cumulative_edit_density diverges > 25% from transition_density target
details.primary: adjust upcoming pacing - too dense: lengthen next 3-4 holds by 20-30%; too sparse: shorten next 3-4 holds by 15-20%
antiPatterns: Distribute adjustment - don't make one shot extremely long/short
Don't correct during montage_mode
Don't correct in hook or closing zones
