nodes.name: Visual Clutter Reduction
nodes.summary: Stagger or remove overlays when more than 2 non-caption elements overlap, preventing Gestalt figure-ground confusion.

details.trigger: active_overlays_count > 2 (excluding captions) AND overlap > 1s
details.primary: stagger_overlays (delay newest until existing one exits + 0.3s)
complements: if staggering impossible: remove lowest-priority overlay
priority: caption > stat graphic > lower third > callout > keyword > other
antiPatterns: Never 3+ non-caption overlays simultaneously
Never spatially overlapping overlays
Exception: caption + ONE other is acceptable

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - perception constraint

details.why: Gestalt figure-ground - multiple figures = perceptual confusion. The viewer reads NONE effectively.
details.learningTarget: overlay tolerance per brand
details.detectionHint: at each frame -> count non-caption overlays -> if > 2 AND duration > 1s -> stagger/remove.

nodes.name: Zoom Budget Enforcement
nodes.summary: Hard cap on zoom count forcing selectivity since over-zooming is the primary 'AI-edited' tell and scarcity increases impact.

details.trigger: zoom_count >= zoom_budget
details.primary: suppress_zoom (all subsequent zoom triggers ignored)
complements: weight > 0.9 can override ONE budget limit (logged as budget_exceeded)
antiPatterns: Don't exceed silently - log when reached
Don't retroactively remove earlier zooms

weightResponse.high: Budget is hard cap. Weight > 0.9 can override once (with logging)

details.why: Over-zooming = 'AI-edited' tell. Budget forces selectivity. Scarcity increases impact.
details.learningTarget: zoom_budget itself
details.detectionHint: running zoom_count -> check count < budget -> if at limit, skip unless weight > 0.9.

nodes.name: Charged Silence Protection
nodes.summary: Override silence removal and pacing tolerance when narrative pressure is high, protecting intentional dramatic silence as emphasis.

details.trigger: narrative_pressure > 0.6 AND silence_duration > silence_tolerance - silence that WOULD be flagged as dead air, but narrative context says it's intentional
details.primary: PROTECT_SILENCE (override silence removal AND pacing_tolerance) - silence stays. Shot holds. System does NOTHING.
complements: ambient: minimum room tone (-35 to -40dB)
caption: hold last word or '...'
zoom: maintain current level, don't change
antiPatterns: NEVER remove silence when narrative_pressure > 0.6
NEVER add SFX, graphics, or elements to fill charged silence
NEVER cut away from charged silence
Cap hold at moment_weight x 5 seconds max (0.9 = 4.5s, 0.7 = 3.5s)

weightResponse.high: moment_weight directly determines max silence duration: 0.9 = 4.5s
weightResponse.low: Below 0.5: narrative_pressure unlikely to reach 0.6, so mapping rarely fires

details.why: Tarkovsky's time-pressure applied to commercial content. The pause after a strong claim IS the emphasis. The viewer is processing. Filling it robs them of that processing.
details.learningTarget: narrative_pressure threshold (0.6 may need adjustment)
details.detectionHint: BEFORE silence_removal or pacing_exceeded fires -> check narrative_pressure -> if > 0.6, BLOCK. This mapping has PRIORITY over pacing/silence mappings.

nodes.name: Montage Mode Activation
nodes.summary: Switch to metric montage rules with beat-locked cuts and uniform transition types when montage mode activates.

details.trigger: montage_mode = true
details.primary: switch to montage rules: cuts metric (beat-locked, every 1-2 beats), transitions ALL same type within run (all hard cuts OR all whip-pans OR all flash - not mixed), pacing_tolerance overridden to BPM/60 seconds
complements: transitions become performative (ARE the content, not connectors)
entry on chorus/drop: zoom punch or flash
color: can shift more dramatically between shots
antiPatterns: Don't mix transition types within montage
Don't add text overlays during fast montage (unreadable)
Exit gracefully when speech_energy rises > 0.3 or music section changes

weightResponse.high: Binary - active or not. Weight affects entry impact (higher = more dramatic entry)

details.why: Eisenstein's metric montage. In music-driven content, the editing rhythm IS the experience. Uniform transitions create a pattern the viewer entrains to.
details.learningTarget: transition type preference, beat division (every beat vs every other)
details.detectionHint: montage_mode composite -> if true, override pacing with beat-locked timing -> enforce uniform transitions -> monitor exit conditions.

nodes.name: Cinematic Moment Emphasis
nodes.summary: Apply strongest multi-technique treatment (2-3 techniques) when 2+ analysis tracks peak within 500ms, creating unified chills moments.

details.trigger: cinematic_moment = true (2+ tracks peak within 500ms)
details.primary: multi_technique_emphasis (2-3 complementary techniques): zoom_punch OR zoom_push, SFX impact or stinger, caption_emphasis
complements: should be STRONGEST treatment in the video
if only cinematic moment: maximum. If multiple: highest-scored gets maximum, others moderate
antiPatterns: Max 3 techniques simultaneously
Max 3 cinematic moments per minute
Can override ONE budget limit if budget exhausted

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: zoom punch + SFX + caption + possible flash
weightResponse.medium: 0.7-0.9: zoom push + SFX + caption; 0.5-0.7: zoom push + caption

details.why: Multi-sensory peak convergence = strongest emotional moments. Unified signal across all channels. The 'chills' moment.
details.learningTarget: emphasis intensity ceiling per brand
details.detectionHint: existing five-track cinematic moment detection -> route through moment_weight -> apply technique stack.

nodes.name: Reaction Moment Cut
nodes.summary: Cut to listener's face during speaker pause with extended hold, exploiting mirror neuron activation that's stronger for reactions than actions.

details.trigger: reaction_moment = true (speaker A stops + person B emotion shift)
details.primary: cut_to_listener (show person B's face, hold 2-4s)
complements: hold longer than normal (K-drama reaction hold 3-5s)
zoom_push (subtle, 1.0x -> 1.05x on listener)
L-cut: hear speaker's next line but stay on listener 1-2s before cutting back
antiPatterns: Don't cut to neutral face (no visible reaction - adds nothing)
Don't cut mid-sentence of speaker
Max 2-3 reaction cuts per minute
Until PHASE_2: LOW CONFIDENCE - suggest only, don't auto-apply

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: extended hold (4-5s) + L-cut

details.why: Gallese & Guerra (2012) - mirror neurons activate more for REACTIONS than actions. Viewer empathizes with the receiver. Fincher's deposition, K-drama signature.
details.learningTarget: hold duration, frequency
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] Grok + V-JEPA face tracking -> emotion delta after speech ends -> trigger. Until Phase 2: approximate with silence + face_present + heuristic.

nodes.name: Speaker Delivering Key Point
nodes.summary: Combined treatment when 4 signals converge in 3s: high energy, slow rate, emphasis word, and build/climax phase - the editorial highlighter.

details.trigger: ALL within 3s window: speech_energy > energy_baseline + 0.15, speaking_rate < baseline * 0.9, emphasis_word detected, narrative_phase = build or climax
details.primary: zoom_push (1.0x -> 1.12x, 2-3s)
complements: caption emphasis on emphasized words
if entity_number: stat_graphic (ideal placement)
music: supportive, duck if needed
antiPatterns: Should fire relatively rarely (2-4 per 3-minute video)
If within 10s of previous key_point: skip or reduce intensity
Don't combine with zoom_punch - push is enough

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: full treatment

details.why: Simultaneous high energy + slow rate + emphasis = speaker delivering core message. The editorial highlighter.
details.learningTarget: threshold sensitivity - how many simultaneous signals needed
details.detectionHint: check 3s window -> count matching conditions -> if >= 4, fire.

nodes.name: Energy Momentum Building
nodes.summary: Progressive pacing increase over 15-20s when multiple signals rise simultaneously, building toward a peak that must resolve.

details.trigger: over 15-20s, MULTIPLE rising signals: speech_energy_delta positive trend, music_energy rising, speaking_rate increasing
details.primary: progressive_pacing_increase - shorten holds by 5-10% per shot, zoom slightly tighter each shot, increase graphic/SFX likelihood
antiPatterns: Don't accelerate too quickly - natural, not frantic
Build MUST resolve within 20s (cinematic_moment or drop) - viewer feels cheated otherwise
Don't build if content doesn't support it

weightResponse.high: Build modulated by destination's weight - climax at 0.9 = aggressive build

details.why: Rising energy across channels creates anticipation. The viewer's body tenses. The edit maintains trajectory without prematurely releasing.
details.learningTarget: build rate - how aggressively to escalate
details.detectionHint: 15-20s trend lines for speech/music/rate -> if 2+ positive and sustained -> activate progressive adjustment.

nodes.name: Interview Dialogue Rhythm
nodes.summary: Apply dialogue editing pattern with J/L-cuts and reaction shots when multiple speakers alternate in formal content.

details.trigger: speaker_change > 2 per minute AND has_multiple_speakers AND formality > 0.4
details.primary: dialogue_editing_pattern - cut to new speaker within 0.5-1.5s of starting, alternate following conversation rhythm, J-cuts for anticipation (hear new speaker 0.3-0.5s before seeing), L-cuts for reaction (keep hearing previous while showing listener)
complements: wider 'master' shot every 30-45s for orientation
strong points: hold on listener's reaction
antiPatterns: Don't cut at exact speech start every time (metronomic)
Don't stay on one speaker > 15s without cutaway
Hard cuts only in dialogue - dissolves slow conversation

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: more reaction cuts, more J/L-cuts (Fincher-style)
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: minimal cutting, mostly stay on speaker

details.why: Dialogue editing has its own rhythm. The editor interprets the conversation - sometimes story is in speaker, sometimes in listener.
details.learningTarget: cut timing after speaker_change, J/L-cut frequency
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] Grok diarization -> compute rhythm -> apply pattern. Until Phase 2: detect from transcript alternation.

nodes.name: Product Demonstration Focus
nodes.summary: Extend hold time and tighten framing during product demonstrations because fast cuts prevent evaluation of highest-intent content.

details.trigger: action_type = demonstrating AND has_product AND speech describes product
details.primary: prefer tighter shots on product during demo - hold longer than pacing_tolerance (extend by 40-50%)
complements: zoom_push toward product during key demo moment
step numbers or feature names from transcript (not AI-generated)
subtle interaction SFX (click, tap)
antiPatterns: Don't cut away during active demo - viewer loses reference
Don't overlay on top of product
Don't use fast pacing - demos need processing time

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: tight focus, step graphics, slow deliberate pacing

details.why: Product demos are highest-intent content. Viewer wants to SEE the product work. Fast cuts and overlays PREVENT evaluation.
details.learningTarget: demo pacing, overlay density
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] V-JEPA 'demonstrating' + has_product -> extend tolerance. Until Phase 2: transcript keywords ('let me show you', 'as you can see').

nodes.name: Organic Imperfection Injection
nodes.summary: Final pass adding controlled micro-variations to prevent detectable machine precision, mimicking a human editor's natural feel.

details.trigger: FINAL PASS - after all other mappings applied. Detection: signs of machine precision: all cuts within +/-1 frame of beats for 6+ consecutive, all shot durations within 5% of each other for 5+ shots, all zooms at exactly same scale, all transitions exactly same duration
details.primary: humanize - +/-2-3 frame jitter on cuts (seeded by projectId), vary shot durations +/-10-15%, vary zoom targets +/-2-3%, vary transition durations +/-10%
antiPatterns: Don't humanize montage_mode (metric montage SHOULD be precise)
Don't jitter cuts away from speech boundaries
Don't vary so much rhythm feels random - controlled imperfection, not chaos

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - post-processing quality pass

details.why: Professional editors have micro-variations +/-2-3 frames. The editing equivalent of a musician's 'feel.' Perfect precision is detectable and creates uncanny 'too clean' quality.
details.learningTarget: jitter amount per brand - tighter or looser feel
details.detectionHint: after full pipeline -> scan for machine-precision patterns -> apply seeded jitter -> verify no mid-word cuts.

nodes.name: Transition Default Hard Cut
nodes.summary: The invisible baseline transition for 80-90% of all cuts, requiring no justification and communicating simple temporal continuity.

details.trigger: any cut point where no other transition mapping fires
details.primary: hard_cut - the most common transition in any professionally edited video (80-90% of all cuts), says 'the next thing happens' - it's the invisible conjunction
complements: ambient_crossfade (0.1-0.3s - see ambient_continuity_at_cuts mapping)
eye-trace continuity: if subject at frame-right in outgoing shot, prefer subject at frame-left in incoming
antiPatterns: Hard cut is NEVER wrong for basic scene continuation - it's the safe default
Don't override to a 'fancier' transition to make the video feel more 'produced' - that's amateur instinct

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - hard cut is the neutral baseline
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - hard cut is the neutral baseline
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - hard cut is the neutral baseline

details.why: Murch's 'invisible cut' - the best edit is one the viewer doesn't notice. Hard cuts are invisible when they respect emotion, story, and rhythm (Rule of Six priorities). Every other transition TYPE draws attention to itself, which is sometimes desirable but must be earned.
details.learningTarget: N/A - the default is the default
details.detectionHint: if no other transition mapping triggers for this cut point -> hard_cut.

nodes.name: Transition Dissolve
nodes.summary: Temporal ambiguity blend for reflective topic shifts, time passages, or dreamy scenes - blocked when color/motion would create ugly blends.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) topic_boundary AND emotional_arc = 'contemplative' or 'reflective' AND NOT high_motion, B) time_passage_implied = true (detected from transcript), C) scene_type changes AND energy level LOW (energy_baseline < 0.4) AND pacing_tolerance > 5. Duration: 0.5-1.5s. BLOCKING CONDITIONS: color_temperature delta > 1000K, motion_intensity > 0.5, montage_mode = true, both clips have strong geometric compositions
details.primary: dissolve (0.5-1.5s, shorter for subtle, longer for dreamy)
complements: audio: crossfade matching dissolve duration (not just ambient - music and speech also blend)
optional: subtle shimmer or tone SFX during dissolve
antiPatterns: Don't dissolve between shots with contrasting emotional tones
Don't dissolve within a montage sequence (breaks momentum)
Max 3-4 dissolves per minute of content - more feels indecisive
Don't dissolve between talking-head shots of the same speaker (looks like a glitch)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: longer dissolve (1-1.5s) for dreamy, weighted feel
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: consider whether dissolve is justified at all - at low importance, hard cut is usually better

details.why: Dissolve creates temporal ambiguity - the viewer's brain interpolates a gap between the two images. This is why it reads as 'time passing' - the blend IS the time. Same cognitive mechanism as dream imagery - soft boundaries between states. But when the two images clash (different moods, clashing colors, high motion), the blend creates confusion rather than poetry.
details.learningTarget: dissolve frequency, duration preferences per brand
details.detectionHint: check transition type selection conditions -> verify NO blocking conditions -> apply dissolve with computed duration.

nodes.name: Transition Fade To Black
nodes.summary: Visual chapter break providing cognitive reset at major narrative shifts, giving the brain processing time between emotional states.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) narrative_phase = resolve AND next scene is narrative_phase = opening (chapter break), B) topic_boundary with cosine delta > 0.5 AND position_in_video 0.3-0.85, C) emotional_valence shifts from strong to opposite abruptly. Duration: 0.3-0.8s to black + 0.3-0.5s hold + 0.3-0.5s from black
details.primary: fade_to_black with hold on black for processing time
complements: audio: fade to silence or near-silence during black, then new audio fades in
the black IS a beat - it gives the viewer processing time between emotional states
antiPatterns: Max 2-3 per video (more = too many chapter breaks)
NEVER in a montage (kills momentum entirely)
NEVER within the first 10% of video (haven't earned a chapter break yet)
Don't use as a substitute for a hard cut
Don't fade to black before the closing zone - that IS the closing zone treatment

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - fade-to-black is structural, not intensity-based
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - fade-to-black is structural, not intensity-based
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - fade-to-black is structural, not intensity-based

details.why: Black is the visual equivalent of silence. It says 'stop processing the previous thing.' It gives the brain a reset - Zacks' event segmentation theory says the brain NEEDS these perceptual boundaries at major narrative shifts. The black is the boundary. Using it for minor shifts trivializes it.
details.learningTarget: when to use vs hard cut for major topic shifts - brand/user preference
details.detectionHint: check for major narrative break conditions -> verify max count not exceeded -> apply with duration.

nodes.name: Transition Whip Pan
nodes.summary: Fast directional transition with mandatory whoosh SFX for high-energy moments, comedic beats, or montage sequences in casual content.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) montage_mode = true AND selected uniform transition type = whip_pan, B) energy spike: speech_energy_delta > 0.3 upward OR music_section just entered chorus/drop AND formality < 0.5, C) comedic beat: rapid topic change + casual tone. Duration: 0.2-0.4s. Direction: match screen_direction of motion or gaze
details.primary: whip_pan (0.2-0.4s, direction matches outgoing shot motion/gaze)
complements: SFX: whoosh ALWAYS (whip-pan without whoosh feels broken - Chion's synchresis)
whoosh direction should match pan direction
whoosh timing: starts 2-3 frames before visual blur, peaks at mid-point, ends 2-3 frames after
antiPatterns: Don't whip-pan if formality > 0.7 (feels uncontrolled in formal content)
Don't mix whip-pan with other fancy transitions in the same 15s window
Don't whip-pan during dialogue (disorienting)
Max 3-4 per video outside montage (becomes a gimmick)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: whip-pan is justified for high-energy moments
weightResponse.medium: 0.5: only if montage_mode or clear energy spike
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: almost never appropriate - use hard cut

details.why: Whip-pan says 'QUICK - look at this!' It's the visual equivalent of someone grabbing your head and turning it. The speed creates urgency, the blur between shots compresses time to zero, and the whoosh provides the physical sensation of rapid movement. Only works when the content justifies that urgency.
details.learningTarget: frequency, direction conventions per brand
details.detectionHint: check energy/montage conditions -> compute direction from screen_direction -> pair with whoosh SFX -> verify formality allows it.

nodes.name: Transition Flash
nodes.summary: 2-4 frame white flash for maximum visual impact at music drops or cinematic peaks, with strict epilepsy safety constraints.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) music_drop_impact fires AND selected technique = flash, B) high impact moment: cinematic_moment peak_score > 0.8 AND formality < 0.6, C) 'snapshot' or 'memory' aesthetic from creative intent. Duration: 2-4 frames of white (66-133ms at 30fps)
details.primary: flash_transition (2-4 frames white)
complements: SFX: shutter click, burst, or impact hit at the flash
can be combined with a cut (flash BRIDGES the cut - viewer doesn't see the splice)
antiPatterns: NEVER more than 3 flashes per second (photosensitive epilepsy risk - WCAG accessibility)
NEVER flash that covers > 25% of screen area for > 3 consecutive flashes
Max 2-3 per video outside montage
Don't flash on formal/serious content - reads as frivolous

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: flash is justified for peak impact moments
weightResponse.low: 0.5-: avoid - hard cut or zoom_punch instead

details.why: A flash creates a visual 'impact' - like a camera flashbulb or lightning strike. It says 'THIS MOMENT' with maximum visual force. The brief white resets the viewer's visual processing, so the incoming shot registers as completely fresh. But it's aggressive and attention-demanding - overuse creates fatigue and epilepsy risk.
details.learningTarget: flash frequency tolerance per brand, flash vs zoom_punch preference
details.detectionHint: check trigger conditions -> verify accessibility limits (count flashes in last 1s) -> apply 2-4 frame white -> pair with SFX.

nodes.name: Transition Wipe
nodes.summary: Explicitly visible stylistic transition for playful/comparative content or east-Asian culture targeting, referencing Star Wars era cinema.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) content_signals.target_culture = east-asian or playful AND formality < 0.4, B) comparison content: two items shown sequentially, C) montage_mode AND selected uniform transition = wipe AND music is upbeat/playful. Direction: left-to-right (Western reading direction). Duration: 0.3-0.6s
details.primary: wipe (directional, 0.3-0.6s)
complements: SFX: whoosh matching wipe direction and speed
wipe edge can be soft (feathered) or hard depending on formality
antiPatterns: Don't wipe on formal/serious content (reads as retro or childish)
Don't mix wipe directions within a sequence
Max 3-4 per video (gimmick fatigue)

weightResponse.high: Not strongly weight-dependent - wipe is a stylistic choice, not an intensity choice
weightResponse.medium: Not strongly weight-dependent - wipe is a stylistic choice, not an intensity choice
weightResponse.low: Not strongly weight-dependent - wipe is a stylistic choice, not an intensity choice

details.why: Wipe explicitly says 'NEW SCENE, different energy.' It's the most visible transition - the viewer always notices it. This visibility makes it playful and retro (Star Wars used wipes extensively). In modern content, it reads as intentionally stylized - which works for certain brands and feels dated for others.
details.learningTarget: whether this brand's aesthetic permits wipes at all
details.detectionHint: check trigger conditions -> compute direction -> pair with directional whoosh -> verify style compatibility.

nodes.name: Transition J-Cut
nodes.summary: Audio of incoming clip leads video by 0.3-0.8s creating anticipation through predictive processing - the sound pulls the visual change.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) scene transition where incoming scene has distinctive audio (new speaker, new music, new ambient), B) speaker_change imminent (incoming speaker's audio starts 0.3-0.5s before visual), C) narrative anticipation moment: viewer should HEAR what's coming before seeing it. Implementation: audio of incoming clip begins 0.3-0.8s before the video cut
details.primary: j_cut (audio leads video by 0.3-0.8s)
complements: the audio 'pull' creates anticipation - the viewer's brain asks 'what am I about to see?'
works especially well when incoming audio is intriguing or surprising
antiPatterns: Don't J-cut if incoming audio is unremarkable (just room tone or continuation of same music)
Don't J-cut longer than 1s (disconnect becomes confusing rather than anticipatory)
Don't J-cut into silence (there IS no incoming audio to lead with)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: J-cut with 0.5-0.8s audio lead (more anticipation)
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: hard cut (J-cut not justified at low importance)

details.why: The J-cut leverages the brain's predictive processing - hearing a new sound triggers the prediction 'I'm about to see the source of that sound.' The 0.3-0.8s gap between hearing and seeing creates a micro-moment of anticipation. It makes the cut feel MOTIVATED - the sound PULLED the visual change.
details.learningTarget: J-cut frequency, lead duration per brand
details.detectionHint: at scene boundaries -> analyze incoming clip's first 1s of audio -> if distinct from outgoing audio -> offset video cut 0.3-0.8s after audio transition.

nodes.name: Transition L-Cut
nodes.summary: Outgoing audio lingers 0.3-0.8s past visual cut creating emotional continuity - the feeling extends past the visual boundary.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) emotional moment ending: speaker finishes a moving statement AND next shot is different, B) returning from B-roll or cutaway back to speaker: keep B-roll audio 0.3-0.5s into speaker shot, C) closing_zone: let last speaker's words carry over closing visuals/end card. Implementation: audio of outgoing clip continues 0.3-0.8s after video cut
details.primary: l_cut (audio lingers 0.3-0.8s past video cut)
complements: lingering audio creates emotional continuity - the feeling extends past the visual change
works particularly well when outgoing audio is emotional (voice catching, powerful statement, resonant music note)
antiPatterns: Don't L-cut if outgoing audio is trivial (trailing off, filler, or dead air)
Don't L-cut longer than 1.5s (audio and video feel disconnected)
Don't L-cut into a scene with competing audio - the overlap becomes noise

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: L-cut with 0.5-1.0s audio linger (the feeling should STAY)

details.why: The L-cut lets a moment breathe past its visual boundary. When you hear someone's last words while already seeing the next image, the words gain WEIGHT - they're echoing in your mind as the new visual provides context. It's the editing equivalent of a thought lingering after the conversation has moved on.
details.learningTarget: L-cut frequency, linger duration, when emotional weight justifies it
details.detectionHint: at scene boundaries -> analyze outgoing clip's emotional content -> if speech_energy was high or emotional_valence was strong -> extend outgoing audio past video cut by 0.3-1.0s.

nodes.name: Slow Motion Beauty Moment
nodes.summary: Apply 50-75% speed to high-weight graceful physical actions during non-speech moments, adding temporal weight and savoring.

details.trigger: ALL of: moment_weight > 0.7, speech_energy < 0.2 (no one talking), motion_intensity between 0.3-0.7, action_type involves physical grace (walking, pouring, falling, flowing, dancing, product interaction), NOT ai_artifact_risk > 0.3. Duration: 1.5-4s of slow-mo
details.primary: slow_motion (50-75% speed) - source must be higher FPS than output, or AI frame interpolation applied. If 30fps source/output: 75% slowest acceptable. If 60fps source: 50% looks good
complements: audio: replace with music swell or etherealized ambient (original audio unusable at reduced speed)
color: slight warm shift or saturation increase during slow-mo
exit from slow-mo should be a cut, not a speed ramp back
antiPatterns: NEVER slow-mo speech (sounds demonic/alien)
NEVER slow-mo AI-generated footage (temporal artifacts become extremely visible)
NEVER slow-mo 24fps source below 80% without frame interpolation
Don't slow-mo mundane actions (walking to a desk, typing)
Max 2-3 slow-mo moments per 3-minute video
Don't slow-mo shots longer than 4s

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: 50% speed with full complement (color, music swell)
weightResponse.low: 0.7-: consider whether slow-mo is justified - at lower weights, normal speed is usually better

details.why: Slow-motion adds 'weight' to a moment by giving the viewer more time to absorb visual detail. The brain interprets temporal stretching as importance - 'this moment is being savored.' It mimics the subjective experience of time slowing during peak emotional moments.
details.learningTarget: speed percentage, frequency, which action types warrant it per brand
details.detectionHint: check all trigger conditions -> verify FPS is sufficient -> apply speed reduction -> replace audio -> apply color complement -> schedule exit cut.

nodes.name: Speed Ramp Emphasis
nodes.summary: Temporal squash-and-stretch using speed ramps (100% to 50-75% to 100%) for physical emphasis at transitions or action highlights.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) transition between energy states: low -> high (ramp fast at impact) or high -> low (ramp slow at resolution), B) cinematic_moment approaching: build normal -> hit moment -> momentarily slow -> resume, C) action highlight: action_type = physical motion AND moment_weight > 0.7
details.primary: speed_ramp - normal (100%) -> slow (50-75%) -> normal (100%) over 1-3 seconds total, OR normal -> fast (130-150%) -> normal for energy compression. Ramp curve should ease (not linear)
complements: SFX: whoosh or 'time-stretch' sound aligned to speed change
the slow point should align with the peak moment (emphasis_word, action peak, beat)
zoom_push can compound with speed ramp (push during slow phase = maximum emphasis)
antiPatterns: Don't speed-ramp during dialogue (speech becomes unintelligible)
Don't speed-ramp AI footage to slower than original (artifact amplification)
Speed-ramp UP (fast) is safer on AI footage - compresses artifacts
Don't stack with other emphasis techniques at the same moment
Max 1-2 per video outside montage

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: deep ramp (100% -> 50% -> 100%) with full SFX + zoom

details.why: Disney's 'squash and stretch' principle applied to time. Speed ramps create a physical sensation - the viewer feels the deceleration in their body. The slow phase says 'look at THIS.' The return to normal says 'moving on.' It's temporal emphasis - the editing equivalent of bold text.
details.learningTarget: ramp depth and duration per brand, frequency tolerance
details.detectionHint: detect trigger condition -> compute ramp curve (ease-in/ease-out) -> align slow-point to peak moment -> pair with SFX -> verify not during speech.

nodes.name: Time Lapse Process
nodes.summary: Compress 30-120s of process footage into 3-8s at 200-1000% speed to respect viewer time while showing work occurred.

details.trigger: ALL of: content shows a process that takes time (construction, cooking, assembly, travel, setup), speech_energy < 0.2 sustained, duration of process footage > 15s at normal speed, formality < 0.7
details.primary: time_lapse (200-1000% speed depending on process duration) - target: compress 30-120s real time into 3-8s screen time, speed consistent throughout
complements: music: energetic or playful during time-lapse
SFX: optional rapid ticking, mechanical whir, or sped-up ambient
entry into time-lapse should be a CUT (hard transition from normal to fast)
exit should also be a cut back to normal speed
antiPatterns: Don't time-lapse facial close-ups (faces at high speed look comical unless intentional)
Don't time-lapse with speech occurring (compressed speech is gibberish)
Don't time-lapse scenes with no visible change (static shot sped up = same static shot)
Don't vary the speed within a time-lapse (looks like a technical error)

weightResponse.high: Not strongly weight-dependent - time-lapse is a functional technique, not emotional
weightResponse.medium: Not strongly weight-dependent - time-lapse is a functional technique, not emotional
weightResponse.low: Not strongly weight-dependent - time-lapse is a functional technique, not emotional

details.why: Time-lapse says 'a process happened, here's the summary.' It respects the viewer's time by compressing the boring parts while showing that the work occurred. The speed ITSELF communicates 'this took time but we're not making you wait.'
details.learningTarget: compression ratio (how fast), whether brand uses time-lapse at all
details.detectionHint: detect process content from transcript/visual analysis -> compute compression ratio from source duration -> apply uniform speed-up -> replace audio -> hard cut entry/exit.

nodes.name: Ambient Bed Construction
nodes.summary: Continuous ambient bed for every scene matched to scene type, creating the audio 'place' that makes video feel like it exists in a real world.

details.trigger: EVERY scene in EVERY video (ambient is never optional)
details.primary: select and place ambient bed layer matching scene_type: indoor_office: soft HVAC hum (-28 to -24dB), indoor_home: room tone (-30 to -26dB), indoor_studio: clean room tone (-32 to -28dB), outdoor_urban: traffic (-24 to -20dB), outdoor_nature: birds/wind (-26 to -22dB), outdoor_crowd: crowd walla (-22 to -18dB), abstract/graphic: minimal tone (-32 to -28dB). Duration: continuous throughout scene
complements: ambient bed should be FELT, not heard - if viewer notices ambient, it's too loud
for Mode 1 (AI footage): CRITICAL - AI clips have zero audio. Ambient IS the reality layer
for Mode 2 (raw footage): use production audio's ambient where possible, supplement if thin
antiPatterns: NEVER leave a scene without ambient (true digital silence = technical error)
Don't use outdoor ambient on indoor scenes or vice versa
Don't use recognizable/distracting ambient (specific song, identifiable voice)
Don't loop ambient beds shorter than 30s without crossfade (audible loop point)
Ambient should not compete with speech - duck ambient 3-6dB under dialogue

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - ambient is infrastructure, not creative emphasis
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - ambient is infrastructure, not creative emphasis
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - ambient is infrastructure, not creative emphasis

details.why: Chion's foundational principle - ambient bed creates 'place.' Without it, video feels like it exists in a void. The brain processes ambient subconsciously - when it's absent, something feels wrong even if the viewer can't identify what. Ambient is the audio equivalent of production design - it sets the world that everything else happens in.
details.learningTarget: ambient style preferences per brand (some prefer clean/minimal, some prefer rich/textured)
details.detectionHint: scene_type classifier -> select ambient bed from library (Freesound/R2 cache) -> set level per scene type -> apply continuous with crossfades at boundaries.

nodes.name: Transition Sound Pairing
nodes.summary: Deterministic SFX pairing for every non-hard-cut transition because sound completes the visual event through Chion's synchresis.

details.trigger: EVERY transition that is not a hard_cut - hard cuts get ambient crossfade only, every other transition type REQUIRES a paired sound
details.primary: select SFX matching transition type [DETERMINISTIC pairing]: dissolve: shimmer/tone (-20dB), fade_to_black: parallel audio fade, wipe: directional whoosh (-12 to -15dB), whip_pan: fast whoosh MANDATORY (-10 to -12dB), zoom_punch: impact hit MANDATORY (-8 to -12dB), flash: shutter click/burst (-10 to -14dB), iris: mechanical sound (-18dB), match_cut: sustained tone or silence, speed_ramp: time-stretch sound (-14dB). Timing: frame-accurate (temporal binding window ~200ms, 3 frames is conservative target)
antiPatterns: NEVER leave a transition without its paired sound (except hard cut and match cut)
Don't use the same SFX for different transition types
Don't overpower the transition sound - it should support, not dominate
SFX should not mask speech - if speech is crossing boundary, reduce SFX by 6dB

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: SFX slightly louder and more present

details.why: Chion's synchresis - simultaneous sound + visual = fused percept. A transition without sound feels like something is missing. The viewer doesn't think 'there's no sound' - they think 'that transition felt off.' The sound COMPLETES the visual event. It's not decoration - it's structural.
details.learningTarget: SFX style per transition type per brand (some prefer organic sounds, some prefer designed/electronic)
details.detectionHint: at every non-hard-cut transition -> lookup pairing table -> select SFX from library -> align frame-accurate to transition midpoint -> set level per weight.

nodes.name: Spot SFX For AI Footage
nodes.summary: Add synchresis-matched SFX for visible on-screen actions in AI footage to cross the uncanny valley through audio-visual correspondence.

details.trigger: Mode 1 (script -> video) AND visible on-screen action in AI-generated clip - AI footage has NO natural sound. Visible actions without sound break immersion
details.primary: identify visible actions and add corresponding SFX: footsteps (-15 to -12dB), door/opening (-14 to -10dB), object pickup (-18 to -14dB), pouring liquid (-14 to -10dB), typing (-18 to -14dB), applause (-12 to -8dB), vehicle (-12 to -8dB), nature (-16 to -12dB), fabric/clothing (-22 to -18dB), impact/contact (-12 to -8dB). Timing: align within 2-3 frames of visible action
complements: Foley sounds (fabric, handling, movement) fill the 'small sounds' gap
these make AI footage feel REAL - the viewer's brain tests reality through audio-visual correspondence
antiPatterns: Don't add SFX for actions that aren't clearly visible (guessing = wrong timing)
Don't add SFX if action is ambiguous (sound calls attention to ambiguity)
Don't overdo it - focus on clear, prominent actions
if ai_artifact_risk > 0.5 on hands/objects: skip SFX for that action

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: full Foley layer (footsteps, fabric, handling, impact)
weightResponse.medium: 0.5: key action SFX only (door, pour, object pickup)

details.why: The brain tests 'is this real?' through audio-visual correspondence. Visible action + corresponding sound = 'real.' Visible action + no sound = 'something is wrong, probably fake.' For AI-generated footage, sound design is the primary tool for crossing the uncanny valley. Good Foley makes synthetic footage feel filmed.
details.learningTarget: Foley density - how much spot SFX per scene, which action types per brand
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] V-JEPA action recognition identifies visible actions -> match to SFX library -> align timing. Until Phase 2: Gemini Vision keyframe description -> identify prominent actions -> conservative SFX placement on clear actions only.

nodes.name: SFX For Editorial Moments
nodes.summary: Add physicality to on-screen graphic elements through paired SFX, making editorial decisions feel intentional rather than glitchy.

details.trigger: editorial decisions that benefit from sound reinforcement: A) stat_graphic entrance -> subtle pop/ding (-16 to -14dB), B) lower_third entrance -> subtle slide/type sound (-18 to -16dB), C) zoom_punch -> low impact hit (-14 to -10dB), D) quote_card entrance -> subtle paper/card sound (-18 to -16dB), E) caption emphasis moment -> very subtle click/pop (-20dB), F) chapter transition -> transitional stinger/tone (-12 to -10dB)
details.primary: select and place SFX for editorial graphic entrances
antiPatterns: Don't add editorial SFX to EVERY graphic/overlay - becomes a cacophony
Max 1 editorial SFX per 5 seconds (ears need gaps between designed sounds)
Don't add editorial SFX if speech is active AND energetic - the speech carries the moment
Don't use the same SFX for different element types

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: clear, present SFX for editorial elements
weightResponse.medium: 0.5: subtle SFX for key elements only

details.why: Editorial SFX give on-screen elements 'physicality.' A graphic that appears with a subtle pop feels like it has mass - it EXISTS in the world. A graphic that appears silently feels like a bug or a glitch. The sound says 'this was intentional.'
details.learningTarget: which editorial SFX style per brand (organic, electronic, minimal, none)
details.detectionHint: hook into overlay entrance events -> select SFX from category -> time to entrance frame -> set level based on weight and speech activity.

nodes.name: Initial Grade Selection
nodes.summary: Set base color treatment per project from signal combination with absolute skin tone protection on vectorscope I-line.

details.trigger: project start - set ONCE per project based on creative intent
details.primary: select base color treatment from signal combination: formality>0.7+neutral: clean Rec.709; formality>0.7+warm: restrained +200K; formality<0.4+warm: punchy +400K Instagram; formality<0.4+cool: teal-orange split; positive valence: +100-300K warmer; negative valence: -100-200K cooler; indian culture: richer saturation gold; east-asian: softer pastel; nordic: desaturated cool. ABSOLUTE CONSTRAINT: skin tones on vectorscope I-line (~123 degrees)
complements: grade applied consistently across all scenes
if AI-generated footage: apply GENTLE grade (heavy grading amplifies AI color artifacts)
vignette: subtle (-0.1 to -0.2 stops) for formality > 0.5
antiPatterns: Don't over-grade AI footage - 50% of the grade intensity you'd use on real footage
Don't apply creative LUTs on top of each other
Don't push saturation past +20% (colors clip, especially reds)
Don't apply grade that contradicts the brand

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - grade is set per project, not per moment
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - grade is set per project, not per moment
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - grade is set per project, not per moment

details.why: Color grade creates the emotional WORLD the content lives in. A warm grade says 'this is comfortable, human, inviting.' A cool grade says 'this is professional, precise, serious.' The grade is the first thing the viewer feels - before they process any content, they've already absorbed the emotional atmosphere from the color.
details.learningTarget: grade style per brand - Thompson Sampling learns which grade parameters each brand prefers
details.detectionHint: read creative intent -> compute grade parameters -> apply to all clips uniformly -> verify skin tone compliance -> reduce intensity on AI footage.

nodes.name: Grade Shift At Emotional Change
nodes.summary: Subtle color temperature and saturation adjustment at emotional transitions so the viewer feels the mood change subconsciously.

details.trigger: emotional_valence shifts (detected from speech or music mood change) AND scene transition nearby
details.primary: subtle grade adjustment on incoming scene: positive->negative: cool by 100-200K, reduce saturation 5-10%, increase contrast slightly; negative->positive: warm by 100-200K, lift saturation 5-10%, soften contrast slightly
complements: shift should be subtle enough that viewer FEELS mood change but doesn't notice color changed
if transition is a dissolve: the color shift blends naturally during the dissolve
if transition is a hard cut: shift within 300K of previous
antiPatterns: Don't shift more than 300K at a hard cut (visible as a grading error)
Don't shift color on EVERY scene change - only at genuine emotional transitions
Don't shift if skin tones would be pushed off I-line
Max 2-3 deliberate grade shifts per video

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: more noticeable shift (200K, 10% saturation change)

details.why: Color is the subconscious language of mood. When the content shifts emotionally, a subtle color shift helps the viewer's brain register the change without being told. Film colorists do this routinely - the 'warm act' before the 'cold act.' The viewer never thinks about color - they just feel the world change.
details.learningTarget: shift magnitude, whether this brand uses grade shifts at all
details.detectionHint: emotional_valence change detected -> compute grade delta -> verify skin tone -> apply to incoming scene clips.

nodes.name: Caption Activation
nodes.summary: Activate and configure caption display mode based on platform, formality, and speaking rate - captions ARE the content on sound-off platforms.

details.trigger: project has speech AND either: A) target_platform is sound-off platform (tiktok, reels, linkedin, facebook, twitter), B) user explicitly requested captions, C) formality > 0.5 (professional content for accessibility)
details.primary: activate captions for entire video. Display mode: formality>0.7 AND <160WPM: subtitle mode (2-line phrases); formality 0.4-0.7: phrase mode (3-5 word groups); formality<0.4 AND <180WPM: word-by-word mode (kinetic); >180WPM regardless: phrase mode; formality<0.3 AND energy>0.6: word-by-word with emphasis scaling (Hormozi style)
complements: caption style (font, color, background) matches brand and formality
captions appear 0.25-0.5s before speech (pre-display for reading preparation)
captions disappear 0.25-0.5s after speech ends
antiPatterns: Don't show captions AND full-screen graphics simultaneously
Don't use word-by-word mode when speaking rate > 180 WPM (words flash too fast)
Don't use script/decorative fonts for captions (readability failure)
Don't position captions in platform unsafe zones
Min 1.0s display per caption group. Min 0.08s gap between consecutive groups
Max 42 characters per line, max 2 lines per group

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - caption activation is a content-wide decision
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - caption activation is a content-wide decision
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - caption activation is a content-wide decision

details.why: Accessibility is non-negotiable. Beyond accessibility, captions dramatically increase engagement on sound-off platforms. Word-by-word kinetic captions force reading - the viewer's eyes track the revealing words, creating physical engagement that static subtitles don't achieve.
details.learningTarget: display mode preference per brand, styling preferences
details.detectionHint: check platform + formality + speaking_rate -> select display mode -> compute word/phrase groupings from Whisper timestamps -> position within safe zones -> verify reading speed compliance.

nodes.name: Caption Position Adjustment
nodes.summary: Temporarily reposition captions to avoid spatial overlap with entering graphics since the viewer can only read one text element at a time.

details.trigger: graphic overlay is entering screen AND would overlap with caption position
details.primary: temporarily reposition captions to avoid overlap: if graphic in lower third: move captions to upper safe zone; if graphic is center: move captions to lower third; if both occupied: delay graphic entrance until caption group completes. Duration: reposition persists while overlap exists
antiPatterns: Don't show captions and graphics in the same screen region simultaneously
Don't bounce captions between positions more than twice per 10 seconds (disorienting)
If repositioning would place captions in unsafe zone: delay the graphic instead

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - layout management

details.why: Captions and graphics compete for the same cognitive resource - reading. The viewer can read ONE text element at a time. Two overlapping text elements means they read NEITHER effectively. Spatial separation preserves both.
details.learningTarget: N/A - layout constraint
details.detectionHint: at each overlay entrance -> check spatial overlap with caption region -> if overlap, compute repositioned caption coordinates -> verify new position is in safe zone.

nodes.name: Voiceover Visual Freedom
nodes.summary: Drive visual cuts by narration content rather than speech boundaries when speaker is not visible, creating a visual essay that amplifies.

details.trigger: has_narration = true AND face_present = false (or face_present but NOT the narrator) - VO audio playing over B-roll or illustrative visuals
details.primary: visual cuts driven by CONTENT of narration, not speech boundaries: when VO mentions a concept -> cut to visual that illustrates it; when VO shifts topics -> cut to new visual; when VO builds energy -> increase visual cut density; cuts can happen MID-SENTENCE because viewer is not watching a mouth move
complements: visual rhythm complements VO rhythm but doesn't need to lock to it
B-roll illustrates, contrasts, or metaphorizes what VO is saying
timing: new visual 0.5-1s BEFORE VO mentions the concept (visual priming)
antiPatterns: Don't hold a single B-roll shot for the entire VO duration (viewer gets bored)
Don't cut B-roll so fast viewer can't process what they're seeing
Don't show visuals that contradict the VO content

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: dynamic B-roll changes every 2-3s, tightly illustrating VO content

details.why: Voiceover creates two independent tracks - audio tells the story, visual illustrates it. The editor's job with VO is to create a VISUAL ESSAY that amplifies the narration. The best VO editing has visuals that ADD meaning rather than just redundantly showing what's being described.
details.learningTarget: B-roll density, visual-VO timing offset, illustration vs metaphor preference
details.detectionHint: detect has_narration + no speaker face visible -> switch to VO editing mode -> align visual changes to transcript content keywords -> use content-driven cut timing instead of speech-boundary timing.

nodes.name: On Camera Speech Constraints
nodes.summary: Hard constraints locking visual cuts to speech boundaries when speaker face is visible to preserve the social bond with viewer.

details.trigger: face_present = true AND speech_energy > 0.2 AND eye_contact = true (or gaze toward camera) - the speaker IS the visual
details.primary: visual cuts MUST respect speech boundaries: NEVER cut mid-word (lip sync breaks), NEVER cut mid-gesture that accompanies speech, prefer cuts at clause/sentence boundaries where speaker naturally pauses, all zoom decisions must move slowly enough that face remains sharp
complements: maintain speaker's face within safe composition (headroom, looking room)
if speaker shifts position (leans, stands, sits): cut on the movement (cut_on_action)
antiPatterns: NEVER jump-cut on-camera speech without zoom change to mask it
Don't cut to different angle mid-word (lip sync mismatch)
Don't zoom fast enough to create motion blur on the face

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - these are constraints, not creative choices
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - these are constraints, not creative choices
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - these are constraints, not creative choices

details.why: On-camera speech creates a social bond between viewer and speaker. Any break in the audio-visual lock (mid-word cut, face jump, blur) breaks that social bond. The viewer momentarily stops listening to the CONTENT and notices the EDIT. That's the cardinal sin - the edit became visible.

nodes.name: Chapter Marker Insertion
nodes.summary: Insert 2-3 chapter cards at most significant topic shifts in videos >3min to provide cognitive scaffolding and reset attention.

details.trigger: ALL of: total video duration > 180 seconds (3 minutes), topic_boundary count >= 3 with cosine delta > 0.4, formality > 0.3
details.primary: insert chapter_card at the 2-3 most significant topic_boundaries: text overlay showing section title (derived from transcript - first key phrase of new topic), duration 1.5-3s (enter 0.3s, hold, exit 0.3s), position center or upper-third. Selection: if 5 boundaries exist, select 2-3 with highest cosine deltas
complements: pair with a transition (fade-to-black or dissolve)
music: chapter break should align with music section change
if target_platform = youtube: these become timestamp chapters in description (bonus SEO)

Don't chapter-mark in first 15% or last 15% of video
Chapter card text must come from transcript analysis - never AI-generated titles
Don't interrupt speaker mid-sentence with a chapter card
Don't use chapter cards in content under 3 minutes

weightResponse.high: only boundaries in segments with weight > 0.5 are eligible
weightResponse.medium: only boundaries in segments with weight > 0.5 are eligible
weightResponse.low: low-weight transitions aren't important enough to mark

details.learningTarget: chapter frequency, card style, which boundaries warrant marking per brand
details.detectionHint: count topic_boundaries with delta > 0.4 -> if >= 3 AND duration > 180s -> rank by delta magnitude -> select top 2-3 -> extract chapter title from first sentence of new section -> schedule card at boundary with transition.

nodes.name: Music Duration Fit
nodes.summary: Surgically edit music track to match video duration at musical phrase boundaries, ensuring climax alignment and proper resolution.

details.trigger: selected_bgm_duration != video_duration (with tolerance of +/- 3 seconds)
details.primary: edit the music track to match video duration. If LONGER: Strategy 1 (preferred): find natural loop point, remove repeated section at phrase boundaries; Strategy 2: shorten intro; Strategy 3: fade out early aligned with closing_zone; Strategy 4: cut to outro. If SHORTER: Strategy 1 (preferred): loop a section (>8 bars) with crossfade; Strategy 2: use two complementary tracks. Timing alignment: ending coincides with video's last 2-3s, biggest moment aligns with highest moment_weight, section changes align with scene transitions
antiPatterns: NEVER hard-cut music mid-phrase (audible as a glitch)
NEVER loop a section shorter than 8 bars
NEVER let music end 5+ seconds before video ends
NEVER let music continue at full energy past closing zone
Don't speed up or slow down the music to fit (pitch/tempo change is audible)

weightResponse.high: Music editing is structural - applies uniformly regardless of moment weights
weightResponse.medium: Music editing is structural - applies uniformly regardless of moment weights
weightResponse.low: Music editing is structural - applies uniformly regardless of moment weights

details.why: Music provides the emotional spine of the video. When it ends abruptly, loops awkwardly, or doesn't align with the content's emotional arc, the viewer feels the mismatch even if they can't identify what's wrong. Musical resolution at the video's end creates closure. Musical climax at the content's climax creates amplification.
details.learningTarget: music editing preferences per brand (seamless loops, deliberate fades, multiple tracks)
details.detectionHint: compare bgm_duration to video_duration -> if delta > 3s -> analyze music structure (sections, phrase boundaries, loop points) -> select strategy -> execute at phrase boundaries -> verify climax alignment -> verify ending aligns with closing zone.

nodes.name: Music Climax Alignment
nodes.summary: Align music's peak energy section with the video's highest moment_weight segment so both peak simultaneously creating 1+1=3.

details.trigger: music has a clear climax section (drop, final chorus, peak energy) AND video has a clear highest-weight segment

music resolution after climax should align with content's resolve phase

Don't try to create 2+ music climaxes - pick the most important and align

details.detectionHint: find music peak energy section -> find highest moment_weight segment -> compute time offset -> if > 5s, plan music edit to realign.

nodes.name: Film Grain Texture

details.trigger: formality > 0.5 AND content is not pure graphic/screencast

complements: grain unifies AI-generated footage with real footage (AI clips look too clean)
grain masks minor color grading inconsistencies between clips

Don't add heavy grain (> 8%) - reduces perceived resolution
Don't add grain to text overlays or graphics (reduces readability)
Don't vary grain between shots (inconsistent grain is more distracting than no grain)

weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - grain is a uniform finishing treatment
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - grain is a uniform finishing treatment

nodes.name: Shot To Shot Color Consistency
nodes.summary: Final pass normalizing color metrics between consecutive shots to prevent the 'assembled from different sources' tell.

details.trigger: FINAL PASS - after initial grade applied, after all editing complete
details.primary: compare color characteristics of consecutive shots and normalize: measure average luminance, color balance, saturation, contrast. For each pair: if any metric differs >15%, apply subtle correction on incoming shot. Correction: weighted blend (80% original grade, 20% adjustment toward previous shot)

highlight/shadow consistency across cuts
antiPatterns: Don't match shots that are INTENTIONALLY different (grade_shift_at_emotional_change was deliberate)
Don't match across fade-to-black boundaries
Don't match color on montage_mode sections (rapid cuts forgive color variation)
Don't over-correct - some variation is natural

weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - consistency is a uniform finishing treatment
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - consistency is a uniform finishing treatment

nodes.name: Subtle Vignette

weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - vignette is a uniform finishing treatment
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - vignette is a uniform finishing treatment

nodes.name: Transition Match Cut
nodes.summary: Prestige technique connecting disparate subjects through visual shape/motion rhyme, creating Eisenstein's intellectual montage through editing.

the match should be the ONLY event at this moment (no zoom, no graphic)

Don't match-cut more than 1-2 times per video (prestige technique - overuse trivializes)

weightResponse.medium: 0.6-0.8: only if the match is very clean

nodes.name: Transition Smash Cut
nodes.summary: Intentionally jarring hard cut with maximum contrast between shots for comedy, horror, or advertising before/after moments.

antiPatterns: Don't smash-cut in formal content (formality > 0.7 - jarring reads as error)
Don't smash-cut more than 2 per video (impact from rarity)
Don't smash-cut during speech (speaker would be interrupted - aggressive)

weightResponse.medium: 0.5-0.8: only if contrast is truly dramatic
weightResponse.low: 0.5-: never - smash cut at low importance feels like a mistake

nodes.name: Transition Jump Cut

Don't jump-cut so frequently that speaker position teleports wildly (max 3-4 per 10 seconds)

Don't mix jump-cuts-with-zoom-offset and without-offset in same video

weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - jump cuts are a pacing tool, not emphasis
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - jump cuts are a pacing tool, not emphasis

nodes.name: Transition Invisible Cut
nodes.summary: Hide the splice point behind visual obstruction or motion blur creating a 'one-take' illusion for sophisticated craft signaling.

color: must match exactly across the hidden cut (any shift reveals it)

Don't use if audio can't be made continuous (audio jump reveals the cut)

Max 2-3 per video (impressive but risk breaking if any one fails)

weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - invisible cuts are structural/stylistic
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - invisible cuts are structural/stylistic

nodes.name: Transition Dip To White
nodes.summary: Aspirational/transcendent transition to white for positive reveals, dream sequences, or spiritual content - the opposite of black's gravity.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) content transitions to positive/bright/aspirational moment (product reveal, happy outcome, 'the future'), B) 'flash forward' or 'dream sequence' beginning, C) spiritual/wellness/meditation content transitions, D) flashback ending - returning from memory to present. Duration: 0.2-0.5s to white + 0.1-0.3s hold + 0.2-0.5s from white
details.primary: dip_to_white (fade to white and back)
complements: SFX: bright shimmer, chime, or ethereal tone (not impact - white is soft)
can pair with saturation boost on incoming shot (emerging from white into vivid color)
antiPatterns: Don't dip-to-white on dark/serious content (tonal mismatch)
Don't dip-to-white more than 1-2 per video (novelty technique)
Don't combine with flash (similar but different purposes)
Accessibility: white flash must respect epilepsy guidelines (<3 flashes/sec)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: dip-to-white with shimmer SFX and saturation boost on incoming
weightResponse.low: 0.5-: avoid - hard cut or dissolve instead

details.why: White is the opposite of black in narrative meaning. Black = ending, gravity, death, chapter close. White = beginning, lightness, birth, transcendence. Dipping to white says 'we're emerging into something new and bright.' It's aspirational where black is conclusive.
details.learningTarget: whether brand aesthetic uses white transitions
details.detectionHint: check emotional direction of transition -> if moving toward positive/bright/aspirational -> consider dip-to-white over dip-to-black.

nodes.name: Transition Film Burn

details.primary: film_burn (warm light leak overlay transition, 0.5-1.0s)

SFX: film projector sound, subtle crackle, or warm analog tone
pairs well with overall film grain aesthetic

weightResponse.medium: Not strongly weight-dependent - film burn is stylistic, not emphasis-driven
weightResponse.low: Not strongly weight-dependent - film burn is stylistic, not emphasis-driven

nodes.name: Transition Iris Wipe

details.trigger: ANY of: A) playful/theatrical content with formality < 0.3, B) 'spotlight' moment - iris-in to focus on specific subject/detail, C) ending/conclusion with retro feel (iris-out = classic 'The End'), D) children's content or deliberately playful visual language. Duration: 0.3-0.6s, shape: circular, centered on subject
details.primary: iris_wipe (circular wipe centered on subject position)
complements: SFX: subtle mechanical/optical sound or none
iris-IN (closing to circle on subject): focuses attention
iris-OUT (opening from circle to full frame): reveals new scene

Don't iris more than 1-2 per video
Don't iris-in on off-center subject (circle centers on subject, not frame)

nodes.name: Transition Blur
nodes.summary: Defocus-based transition hiding the cut at peak blur, solving dissolve color-clash problems while simulating natural eye focus shift.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) dreamy/ethereal content AND dissolve would work but clips have color temp mismatch, B) transition from sharp/present reality to memory/imagination, C) depth-of-field motivated: rack focus to blur -> cut while blurred -> rack focus to sharp. Duration: 0.3-0.6s blur out + cut at peak blur + 0.3-0.6s blur in
details.primary: blur_transition (Gaussian blur ramp out -> cut at peak blur -> blur ramp in)
complements: the blur peak is the hide point - cut happens when both shots are maximally blurred
SFX: soft whoosh or ethereal tone during blur
color: can shift during blur (viewer can't see change clearly)
antiPatterns: Don't blur in fast-paced content (blur takes too long, kills momentum)
Don't blur if viewer needs to read text near the transition
Don't stack blur with dissolve (redundant - both are 'soft')
Max 2-3 per video

weightResponse.high: 0.7+: blur with full SFX and color shift
weightResponse.low: 0.5-: avoid - hard cut or dissolve instead

details.why: Blur simulates the eye's natural defocus - when you shift attention between objects at different distances, there's a brief moment of blur. It says 'we're shifting focus' rather than 'we're cutting.' It also solves the dissolve-color-clash problem - blurred color blends are forgiving where sharp blends are ugly.
details.learningTarget: blur depth, duration, usage frequency per brand

nodes.name: Transition Slide
nodes.summary: Directional push transition implying sequence/progression for tutorials, comparisons, and numbered content.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) sequential content: step 1 -> step 2 -> step 3 (direction implies progression), B) comparison content: option A slides off, option B slides on, C) montage_mode AND selected uniform transition = slide AND consistent direction. Direction: left-to-right (progression), right-to-left (regression), up (elevation). Duration: 0.3-0.5s

complements: SFX: directional whoosh matching slide direction
outgoing shot slides OUT while incoming slides IN simultaneously
antiPatterns: Don't mix slide directions within a sequence
Don't slide in formal content without strong justification (reads as PowerPoint)
Don't slide during speech (visual movement is distracting during dialogue)
Max 4-5 per video in sequence, or unlimited in montage with consistent direction

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - slide is sequential/structural

details.why: Slide transitions imply SEQUENCE - the next item pushes the previous off screen. Direction implies progression (left-to-right in Western = forward). Slides are the most 'presentation-like' transition, appropriate for educational/sequential content and wrong for emotional/narrative content.
details.learningTarget: whether brand uses slide transitions, preferred direction
details.detectionHint: detect sequential content pattern -> select consistent direction -> apply push animation.

nodes.name: Transition Soft Cut
nodes.summary: Ultra-short 3-5 frame dissolve that's invisible polish - removes the micro-jolt of hard cut without temporal weight of a full dissolve.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) any cut point where hard cut feels slightly too abrupt but dissolve would be too slow, B) consecutive talking-head shots of same speaker at slightly different angles/scales, C) formality 0.5-0.7 where hard cuts feel too raw and dissolves feel too produced. Duration: 3-5 frames (100-167ms at 30fps)

complements: ambient crossfade (same as hard cut - soft-cut is too brief to need special audio)
antiPatterns: Don't soft-cut in fast-paced content (brief blend creates ghost images at rapid pacing)
Don't soft-cut between shots with very different compositions
Don't confuse with dissolve - soft-cut is <6 frames, dissolve is 15+ frames

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - soft-cut is a subtlety tool
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - soft-cut is a subtlety tool
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - soft-cut is a subtlety tool

details.why: The soft-cut is the 'invisible polish' transition. The viewer can't identify it - they just feel that the cuts are 'smooth.' It removes the micro-jolt of a hard cut without the temporal weight of a dissolve. Used extensively in high-end commercial and documentary editing.
details.learningTarget: soft-cut vs hard-cut preference per brand
details.detectionHint: at cut points where both clips have similar composition and low motion -> apply 3-5 frame opacity crossfade instead of hard cut.

nodes.name: Callout Graphic
nodes.summary: Arrow/line graphic pointing from label to specific on-screen area when speaker references a feature, bridging verbal and visual attention.

details.trigger: speaker is explaining something visible on screen AND pointing to or describing a specific area: A) action_type = demonstrating AND transcript references a specific part/feature, B) product close-up visible AND speaker names a feature
details.primary: callout (arrow or line pointing from label to specific area on screen) - text: feature name from transcript, duration 2-4s, enter 0.3s after feature verbally named
antiPatterns: Don't callout if the referenced area is ambiguous or unclear in the video
Don't stack multiple callouts simultaneously (max 1 at a time)
Don't callout in wide shots where the target area is too small to see
Callout text must come from transcript - never AI-labeled features
Don't callout during fast pacing - needs 2+ seconds to read

weightResponse.high: 0.7+: callout with animation (draw-in line + label fade)
weightResponse.low: 0.5-: skip - the verbal mention is sufficient

details.why: Callouts bridge the gap between what the speaker is SAYING and what the viewer is SEEING. When someone says 'this button here' while showing a complex interface, the callout ensures the viewer finds the right element.
details.learningTarget: callout frequency, style per brand
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] V-JEPA action recognition + object detection -> identify referenced area. Until Phase 2: approximate from transcript keywords ('this,' 'here,' 'the top') + face detection.

nodes.name: Keyword Highlight
nodes.summary: Brief on-screen display of key terms (branded, technical, or repeated) working like bold text to build vocabulary and reinforce branded language.

details.trigger: speaker uses a key term or phrase that should be visually reinforced AND term is: A) branded term or product name (from brief), B) technical term being introduced for first time, C) repeated emphasis phrase (said 2+ times in transcript)
details.primary: keyword_highlight (word/short phrase appears briefly on screen, brand-styled) - text: exact word/phrase from transcript, position: near speaker or center, duration 1.5-2.5s, animation: pop or fade matching formality
antiPatterns: Don't highlight common words ('the,' 'and,' 'this') - only meaningful terms
Don't highlight more than 1 keyword per 15 seconds (keyword fatigue)
Don't highlight and stat-graphic the same content (redundant)
Don't highlight during montage_mode (unreadable at speed)

weightResponse.high: 0.7+: keyword with pop animation and accent color

details.why: Keyword highlights work like bold text in writing - they tell the viewer 'this term matters.' For educational and product content, they help build vocabulary. For brand content, they reinforce branded language through visual repetition.
details.learningTarget: keyword frequency, which terms warrant highlighting per brand
details.detectionHint: NER for branded terms + frequency analysis for repeated phrases + first-mention detection for new terms -> schedule highlight at word timestamp.

nodes.name: Logo Reveal
nodes.summary: Clean brand logo placement in opening (max 2s) or closing (2-4s with end card) using only uploaded brand asset with strict clear space.

details.trigger: position_in_video > 0.90 (final 10%) OR scene_index = first scene (intro logo) AND brand logo asset available in project
details.primary: logo_reveal (branded logo appears, center or lower-right) - intro: 1-2s maximum; outro: 2-4s as part of end card, can combine with CTA; animation: fade-in or scale-up only (no complex animation)
complements: SFX: brand sound logo if available, or subtle branded chime
background: darkened or blurred frame behind logo for contrast
never pair with other graphics - logo gets screen to itself
antiPatterns: NEVER AI-generate the logo - use ONLY uploaded brand asset
NEVER distort, recolor, or animate logo in ways that violate brand guidelines
Don't show logo mid-content unless specifically requested
Don't show intro logo for more than 2s
Maintain clear space (height of tallest letter on all sides) [DETERMINISTIC]
Min size: 48px wide [DETERMINISTIC]
Contrast: 3:1 against background [DETERMINISTIC]

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - logo placement is structural/brand requirement
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - logo placement is structural/brand requirement
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - logo placement is structural/brand requirement

details.why: The logo is the brand's signature. It needs to appear cleanly, clearly, and appropriately - never compromised by creative editing decisions. Less is more with logo presence. A clean 2-second logo at the end communicates more professionalism than an animated logo spectacle.
