nodes.name: Camera Shake Impact
nodes.summary: Brief decaying screen oscillation for maximum physical impact in casual content, triggering the vestibular system to make viewer FEEL the hit.

details.trigger: ANY of: A) cinematic_moment with peak_score > 0.85 AND formality < 0.5, B) music_drop_impact AND selected technique includes physical impact feel, C) comedic emphasis (exaggerated reaction moment)
details.primary: camera_shake (2-4 frame shake, 3-5px displacement, decaying) - very brief (0.1-0.2s), decaying oscillation, simulates physical impact
complements: SFX: impact hit or bass drop (shake without sound feels like a glitch)
zoom_punch can pair (punch + shake = maximum physical impact)
flash (1-2 frames) can precede the shake
antiPatterns: NEVER in formal content (formality > 0.6) - looks like a bug
NEVER during speech - text/captions jump and become unreadable
Max 1-2 per video (extreme technique - overuse is exhausting)
Don't shake for more than 0.3s (longer = earthquake, not impact)
Don't shake during an already-active zoom (competing motions)

weightResponse.high: 0.9+: shake is justified for maximum impact
weightResponse.low: 0.7-: never - too aggressive for moments below high importance

details.why: Camera shake is the most PHYSICAL editing technique - it simulates the viewer's body being rattled by the impact. It's the anime 'impact frame' and the action movie explosion effect. It triggers the vestibular system - the viewer FEELS the shake. Because it's so visceral, it must be used extremely sparingly. One shake in a video is powerful. Three is exhausting.
details.learningTarget: whether brand uses impact techniques, shake intensity
details.detectionHint: check trigger conditions -> generate decaying oscillation (seeded random, 3-5px, 2-4 frames) -> apply as position offset keyframes -> pair with SFX.

nodes.name: Shot Scale Audio Matching
nodes.summary: Adjust ambient and detail sound levels based on visual shot scale to maintain audio-visual perspective matching.

details.trigger: every shot - passive rule that adjusts audio based on visual scale
details.primary: adjust ambient and detail sound levels based on shot_scale: ECU/CU: amplify detail sounds +3-6dB, reduce ambient -3dB (intimate close perspective); MCU/MS: standard balanced levels; WS/EWS: increase ambient +3-6dB, reduce detail -3-6dB (wide environmental perspective)
antiPatterns: Don't play close-up detail sounds on wide shots (sounds impossibly close)
Don't play wide ambient on extreme close-ups (world should feel small and intimate)

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - perceptual consistency rule

details.why: Audio perspective should match visual perspective. In real life, close objects are louder with more detail. Distant objects are quieter with more ambience. When audio and visual perspectives don't match, the brain detects a mismatch. Chion's 'materializing sound indices' - close sounds make close visuals feel tactile.
details.learningTarget: N/A - perceptual consistency rule
details.detectionHint: at each clip -> read shot_scale -> adjust ambient and spot SFX levels proportionally.

nodes.name: Camera Movement Pacing Alignment
nodes.summary: Align cut timing to camera movement completion because cutting mid-movement interrupts the viewer's expectation of arrival.

details.trigger: motion_type = camera_moving AND camera has a direction (push-in, pull-back, pan)
details.primary: align cut timing to camera movement intent: push-in: cut AFTER push completes or at tightest point; pull-back: cut AFTER pull-back reaches widest or at resolution; pan: cut at pan's destination, not mid-pan; tilt: cut at destination; orbit: can cut anywhere in arc (continuous, no destination)
antiPatterns: Don't cut mid-push-in unless interruption is deliberate (smash cut, emergency cut)
Don't cut mid-pan to a static shot - viewer's eye was tracking motion and suddenly stops
Exception: whip-pan transition IS a mid-pan cut by design

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - perceptual alignment rule

details.why: Blain Brown's motivated camera - every camera movement has a PURPOSE and a DESTINATION. Cutting before the movement reaches its destination is like interrupting someone mid-sentence. The viewer was following the motion with an expectation of arrival.
details.learningTarget: N/A - movement-completion rule
details.detectionHint: [PHASE_2] V-JEPA identifies camera movement type and trajectory. Until Phase 2: optical flow direction + magnitude -> if movement is decelerating (approaching destination), good cut point. If accelerating (mid-movement), bad cut point.

nodes.name: Eye Trace Continuity Across Cuts
nodes.summary: Verify eye trace position compatibility (<30% frame diagonal) at every cut to prevent 200-400ms of viewer re-orientation.

details.trigger: EVERY cut point (universal quality rule, like ambient continuity)
details.primary: verify eye_trace_position compatibility. Compatible = distance < 0.3 normalized frame diagonal. If INCOMPATIBLE: Option A (preferred): adjust incoming shot composition in Mode 1; Option B: add brief bridging shot in Mode 2; Option C: accept jump but pair with motivated cut (cut-on-action, whip-pan, or flash) that gives eye 'permission' to relocate
antiPatterns: Don't ignore eye-trace jumps in slow-paced content (most noticeable when viewer has time)
Less critical in fast montage (rapid cuts reset eye trace constantly)
Don't sacrifice emotion (Murch #1) or story (Murch #2) for eye-trace (Murch #4)

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - quality rule, always applied
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - quality rule, always applied
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - quality rule, always applied

details.why: Murch's Rule #4 (7%). When the eye has to jump > 30% of frame width at a cut, the viewer spends 200-400ms re-orienting instead of absorbing the new shot's content. That's 200-400ms of 'where am I?' instead of 'what's happening?' Eye-trace continuity makes cuts INVISIBLE.
details.learningTarget: compatibility threshold (0.3 may need adjustment for different content styles)
details.detectionHint: compute eye_trace_position from outgoing frame -> compute from incoming frame -> measure distance -> if > threshold, flag and apply correction strategy.

nodes.name: Linger Or Leave On Speaker
nodes.summary: Choose whether to cut early (brisk, trust statement) or linger on face after speech (invite scrutiny) based on emotional weight and claim strength.

details.trigger: speech_ends (speaker finishes sentence/thought) AND face_present = true. Decision: CUT EARLY (leave before speaker finishes last 1-2 words) when words are factual/expected/informational (claim_strength=factual, valence=neutral, weight<0.5). LINGER LATE (hold 0.5-2s after speech) when statement is emotionally charged or potentially dishonest, viewer needs to READ THE FACE (valence=strong, claim_strength=assertive, weight>0.7, face_emotion shifting). DEFAULT: standard timing (0.1-0.3s after last word)
details.primary: linger_or_leave decision at speech_end events
antiPatterns: Don't linger after EVERY statement - lingering becomes default and loses power
Don't linger after mundane statements
Don't cut early on emotional statements - viewer needs the face
Max 3-4 deliberate lingers per 3-minute video

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: linger is more likely (high-weight moments benefit from held beat)
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: cut early (low-importance moments should be brisk)

details.why: Murch: 'cutting away before an actor finishes speaking encourages the audience to think only about face value of what was said. Lingering after encourages the audience to question what the character said from their expression.' This changes HOW the viewer interprets content without changing WHAT the content says. Same statement with early cut = trusted. With linger = questioned.
details.learningTarget: linger frequency and duration per brand. Documentary/testimonial brands may want more lingers. Corporate brands may want brisk cuts.
details.detectionHint: at speech_end events -> check emotional_valence, claim_strength, moment_weight -> if strong/assertive/high: schedule linger (hold 0.5-2s past speech end). If neutral/factual/low: schedule early cut.

nodes.name: Post Peak Decompression
nodes.summary: Mandatory breathing room after peaks following Pearlman's breath model - lengthen holds, pull back zoom, reduce density for 5-10s.

details.trigger: cinematic_moment just resolved (peak_score was > 0.7 now declining) OR music_section just transitioned from chorus/drop to verse/bridge OR energy_momentum_building just peaked and speech_energy_delta now negative
details.primary: decompression sequence (opposite of build): lengthen next 2-3 shot holds by 30-50%, zoom_pull_back if currently zoomed (3-5s), reduce graphic density (no new graphics for 5-8s), music should be resolving/quieter, color: subtle warm shift (+100K). Duration: 5-10 seconds before returning to normal pacing
antiPatterns: Don't maintain peak intensity past the peak - viewer exhaustion, diminishing returns
Don't introduce NEW visual elements during decompression
Don't decompress too quickly (1-2s = whiplash). Exhale needs full duration
Exception: if another peak within 10s (double-peak), compress to 3-5s

weightResponse.high: Higher weight peak -> longer decompression. 0.9 peak earned 8-10s of decompression

details.why: Pearlman's breath model. After inhale (tension/build), the body MUST exhale (release). Editing that builds constantly without releasing creates anxiety, not engagement. The decompression makes the NEXT build possible - you can only inhale again after exhaling. Every great editor instinctively provides breathing room after peaks. AI editing without this principle feels relentless and exhausting.
details.learningTarget: decompression duration and intensity per brand
details.detectionHint: after cinematic_moment peak OR music drop resolution -> activate decompression mode for N seconds (based on peak weight) -> suppress zoom/graphic/SFX triggers -> extend shot holds -> schedule pull-back zoom if zoomed.

nodes.name: Sound Defines Meaning For AI Footage
nodes.summary: For AI-generated footage, sound design CREATES emotional meaning rather than accompanying it - the same visual becomes different scenes based on audio.

details.trigger: Mode 1 (script -> video) AND ai_generated_clip = true AND emotional_valence target exists from creative intent
details.primary: design sound to CREATE the emotional meaning, not just accompany it. Same visual with different sound = different meaning. 'warm home': warm room tone + acoustic music + soft fabric SFX. 'tense home': low hum + minor key sparse music + loud metronomic clock + distant creak. The VISUAL is identical. The SOUND determines what the viewer feels.
complements: color grade supports the sound-defined mood (warm sound + warm grade, tense sound + cool grade)
music selection is THE most important decision for AI-generated content
ambient bed is the second most important - places viewer in a WORLD
antiPatterns: Don't leave AI footage with only music - feels like a slideshow. Need ambient + spot SFX
Don't select music that contradicts target emotion in the script
Don't use generic/unmotivated ambient - match scene_type in storyboard

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: full three-layer sound design (ambient + music + spot SFX + feature SFX)

details.why: Chion's 'added value' - sound and image together create an effect greater than either alone. For AI footage, there IS no starting point. The sound design doesn't enhance the image - it DEFINES the image's emotional meaning. Sound is not decoration for AI footage - it's the primary meaning-making channel. This is Chion's core thesis applied to synthetic media.
details.learningTarget: sound design density and style per brand
details.detectionHint: read emotional_valence target from creative intent -> select music mood -> select ambient type matching scene_type -> select spot SFX for visible actions -> layer all three.

nodes.name: Offscreen Sound World Extension
nodes.summary: Add very subtle environmental sounds for things NOT visible to extend perceived world beyond frame edges, leveraging that sound has no frame.

details.trigger: AI-generated footage (Mode 1) OR any footage where visible scene feels spatially limited
details.primary: add environmental sounds for things NOT visible: indoor: distant hallway, muffled conversation next room, elevator ding, HVAC (-24 to -30dB); outdoor urban: distant traffic, far-off siren, construction blocks away; outdoor nature: distant birds, stream off-screen, wind through trees above frame; studio/office: other workstations, distant printer, coffee machine. Level: -24 to -30dB (felt, not heard)
antiPatterns: Don't add off-screen sounds that contradict visible environment (ocean waves in city)
Don't make off-screen sounds louder than on-screen sounds
Don't use recognizable/specific sounds (distinct song, identifiable voice) - stay ambient
Don't overdo it - 2-3 distant environmental elements maximum per scene

weightResponse.high: Not weight-dependent - world extension is a quality/immersion technique
weightResponse.medium: Not weight-dependent - world extension is a quality/immersion technique
weightResponse.low: Not weight-dependent - world extension is a quality/immersion technique

details.why: Chion's insight that 'sound has no frame' - while image is bounded by screen edges, sound extends infinitely. Off-screen sound tells the viewer 'this world continues beyond what you can see.' It transforms a small AI-generated rectangle into a slice of a larger reality. Without it, AI footage feels like it exists in a void.
details.learningTarget: density and style of off-screen sounds per brand/content type
details.detectionHint: read scene_type from storyboard -> select 2-3 distant environmental sounds from library -> set levels very low (-24 to -30dB) -> mix with ambient bed -> ensure no conflicts with visible scene elements.

nodes.name: Deliberate Syncopation
nodes.summary: Intentionally place a cut OFF the beat after 4+ on-beat cuts to create rhythmic tension, applying jazz syncopation principles to editing.

details.trigger: creative intent indicates high energy AND music present with strong rhythmic pulse AND system has been cutting ON beats for 4+ consecutive cuts (pattern established)
details.primary: place the NEXT cut deliberately OFF the beat (between beats, on upbeat, or skip a beat entirely)
complements: off-beat cut should coincide with a visual or speech event (motivated syncopation, not random)
the beat that was 'missed' creates micro-tension that resolves when next cut lands ON beat
can pair with visual hold (no cut where expected = anticipation IS the effect)
antiPatterns: Don't syncopate if viewer hasn't established on-beat pattern first (need 3-4 on-beat cuts before off-beat has effect)
Don't syncopate during montage_mode (montage's power IS metric precision)
Don't syncopate randomly - off-beat placement should still serve emotion or story
Max 1 syncopation per 8-10 beats (too much = no pattern = no tension)

weightResponse.high: 0.8+: syncopation creates powerful emphasis at key moments (beat skips and viewer FEELS it)
weightResponse.low: 0.3-: stay on beat - low importance doesn't warrant attention of syncopation

details.why: Pearlman's pulse theory. Music has a pulse. Editing entrains to that pulse. When cut lands ON pulse, viewer feels stability. When cut lands OFF pulse (syncopation), viewer feels surprise, tension, excitement. Identical to how syncopation works in music - jazz, hip-hop, funk derive energy from playing AGAINST the beat. But syncopation only works when beat has been established first.
details.learningTarget: syncopation frequency and placement style per brand
details.detectionHint: after 4+ consecutive on-beat cuts -> check moment_weight of next beat -> if > 0.7 AND speech/visual event exists between beats -> shift cut to off-beat position. Track beat_alignment_history to ensure pattern established first.
